<margin>Marbas.</margin> *Marbas*, also known as *Barbas*, is a great President and appears in the form of a mighty lion; but at the command of a conjurer, he comes up in the likeness of a man and answers fully regarding anything that is hidden or secret. He brings diseases and cures them; he promotes wisdom and the knowledge of mechanical arts or handicrafts; he changes men into other shapes. Under his presidency or government, thirty-six legions of devils are contained.

<margin>Amon.</margin> *Amon*, or *Aamon*, is a great and mighty Marquess and comes forth in the likeness of a wolf having a serpent's tail, spitting out and breathing flames of fire. When he puts on the shape of a man, he shows dog's teeth and a large head like a mighty raven. He is the strongest prince of all others and understands all things past and to come; he procures favor and reconciles both friends and foes, and rules forty legions of devils.

<margin>Barbatos.</margin> *Barbatos*, a great Count or Earl, and also a Duke, appears in the sign of the Sylvan Archer <note>original: "Signo sagittarii Sylvestris"</note> with four kings, who bring companies and great troops. He understands the singing of birds, the barking of dogs, the lowing of bullocks, and the voice of all living creatures. He detects treasures hidden by magicians and enchanters and is of the Order of Virtues, in which he partly rules. He knows all things past and to come, reconciles friends and powers, and governs thirty legions of devils by his authority.

<margin>Buer.</margin> *Buer* is a great President and is seen in this sign; <note>referring to a specific astrological or magical symbol used to summon him</note> he absolutely teaches moral and natural philosophy, as well as logic and the virtues of herbs. He gives the best familiars, can heal all diseases (especially of men), and reigns over fifty legions.

<margin>Gusoin.</margin> *Gusoin* is a great and strong Duke, appearing in the form of a *Xenophilus* <note>original: "Xenophilus"; likely a corruption of "Xenopilus," meaning a creature with a strange or foreign head</note>. He answers all things—present, past, and to come—explaining all questions. He reconciles friendships and distributes honors and dignities, ruling over forty legions of devils.

<margin>Botis.</margin> *Botis*, otherwise called *Otis*, is a great President and an Earl. He comes forth in the shape of an ugly viper, and if he puts on human shape, he shows large teeth and two horns, carrying a sharp sword in his hand. He gives answers of things present, past, and to come, and reconciles friends and foes, ruling sixty legions.

<margin>Bathin.</margin> *Bathin*, sometimes called *Mathim*, is a great and strong Duke. He is seen in the shape of a very strong man with a serpent's tail, sitting on a pale horse. He understands the virtues of herbs and precious stones, transferring men suddenly from country to country, and rules thirty legions of devils.

<margin>Purson.</margin> *Purson*, also known as *Curson*, is a great King. He comes forth like a man with a lion's face, carrying a most cruel viper and riding on a bear; trumpeters always go before him. He knows hidden things and can tell all things present, past, and to come. He reveals <note>original: "bewrayeth"</note> treasure; he can take a body that is either human or made of air. He answers truly about all things earthly and secret, about divinity and the creation of the world, and brings forth the best familiars. Twenty-two legions of devils obey him, partly from the Order of Virtues and partly from the Order of Thrones.

<margin>Eligor.</margin> *Eligor*, also known as *Abigor*, is a great Duke and appears as a handsome <note>original: "goodly"</note> knight, carrying a lance, a standard <note>original: "Ensign"</note>, and a scepter. He answers fully regarding hidden things and wars, and how soldiers should meet. He knows things to come and procures the favor of lords and knights, governing sixty legions of devils.

<margin>Leraje.</margin> *Leraje*, also known as *Oray*, is a great Marquess, showing himself in the likeness of a gallant archer carrying a bow and a quiver. He is the author of all battles; he causes all wounds made with arrows by archers to rot—making them most severe for three days <note>original: "Quos optimos objicit tribus diebus"</note>—and has command over thirty legions.

<margin>Valefar.</margin> *Valefar*, also known as *Malephar*, is a strong Duke. He comes forth in the shape of a lion with the head of a thief. He is very friendly <note>original: "familiar"</note> with those with whom he makes himself acquainted, until he has brought them to the gallows, and he rules ten legions.

# [Scot's] Discovery of Witchcraft. CHAPTER XI.

<margin>*Morax.*</margin>
**Morax**, also known as *Foraii*, is a great Earl and a President. He appears like a bull, and if he takes on a human face, he makes men incredibly skilled in astronomy and in all the liberal sciences. He provides good and wise familiar spirits and possesses knowledge of the power and virtues of precious herbs and stones. He rules thirty-six legions.

<margin>*Ipos.*</margin>
**Ipos**, also known as *Ayporos*, is a great Earl and a Prince. He appears in the shape of an angel, yet is actually more dark and loathsome than a lion, having a lion’s head, a goose’s feet, and a hare’s tail. He knows things to come and things past; he makes a man clever and bold, and has thirty-six legions under his jurisdiction.

<margin>*Naberius.*</margin>
**Naberius**, also known as *Cerberus*, is a courageous Marquess who shows himself in the form of a crow and speaks with a hoarse voice. He makes a man pleasant and skilled in all arts, especially in rhetoric. He causes the loss of prelacies <note>high offices in the church</note> and dignities. Nineteen legions hear and obey him.

<margin>*Glasya Labolas.*</margin>
**Glasya Labolas**, also known as *Caacrinolaas* or *Caaffimolar*, is a great President who comes forth like a dog and has wings like a gryphon. He grants knowledge of the arts and is the captain of all murderers. He understands things present and to come; he wins the minds and love of both friends and enemies. He can make a man go invisible and rules thirty-six legions.

<margin>*Zepar.*</margin>
**Zepar** is a great Duke who appears as a soldier. He inflames women with love for men, and when he is hidden, he changes their shape until they may enjoy their beloved. He also makes them barren. Twenty-six legions are at his command and obedience.

<margin>*Bileth.*</margin>
**Bileth** is a great and terrible King, riding on a pale horse, preceded by trumpets and all kinds of melodious music. When he is summoned by an exorcist, he appears rough and furious to deceive the conjurer. Therefore, the exorcist or conjurer must take care of himself. To subdue the spirit's courage, he must hold a hazel wand <note>original: "bat"</note> in his hand, reaching out toward the East and South, and draw a triangle outside and next to the Circle. 

But if the spirit does not hold out his hand to the conjurer, and the conjurer bids him enter, yet the spirit still refuses the bond or chain of spirits <note>a magical document or ritual constraint</note>, then let the conjurer proceed with reading the incantations. Immediately, the spirit will submit himself, enter, and do whatever the exorcist commands him, and the exorcist shall be safe. If King Bileth is stubborn and refuses to enter the Circle at the first call, and the conjurer shows himself to be afraid, or if he does not have the "chain of spirits," the demon will certainly never fear or respect him afterward. 

Also, if the location is unsuitable for a triangle to be made outside the Circle, then set a bowl of wine there instead. The exorcist will certainly know when the demon leaves his house with his companions, and that the aforementioned Bileth will be his helper, friend, and obedient to him when he comes forth. When he arrives, the exorcist should receive him courteously and flatter his pride; therefore, he shall show him reverence as other kings do, because he says nothing without the company of other princes. Also, if he is summoned by an exorcist, a silver ring must always be held against the exorcist's face on the middle finger of the left hand, as is done for *Amaimon*. <margin>*See Amaimon.*</margin> The dominion and power of such a great prince is immeasurable, for there is no one under the power and dominion of the conjurer except for him who keeps both men and women in a doting love until the exorcist has had his pleasure. He is of the Order of Powers, hoping to return to the Seventh Throne (which is not entirely believable), and he rules eighty-five legions.

<margin>*Sitri, a lewd Devil.*</margin>
**Sitri**, also known as *Bitru*, is a great Prince who appears with the face of a leopard and has wings like a gryphon. When he takes human shape, he is very beautiful. He inflames a man with a woman's love and also stirs up women to love men. When commanded, he willingly reveals the secrets of women, laughing at them and mocking them to make them lewdly <note>original: "luxuriously"</note> naked; sixty legions obey him.

<margin>*Paimon.*</margin>
**Paimon** is more obedient to **Lucifer** than any other kings are. Lucifer is to be understood here as the one who was overwhelmed by the depth of his own knowledge: he insisted on being like God, and for his arrogance, he was cast out into destruction, of...

<margin>Ezekiel 28:13.</margin>
Of whom it is said, *Every precious stone is your covering.* **Paimon** is forced by divine power to stand before the exorcist, where he takes on the form of a man. He sits upon a beast called a dromedary <note>a swift-running camel</note> and wears a glorious crown. He has a feminine face, and ahead of him goes a host of men with trumpets, well-tuned cymbals, and all kinds of musical instruments. At first, he appears with a great cry and roaring, as is described in the *Circle of Solomon* <note>original: *Circulo Solomonis*</note> and in the Art <note>the "Art" refers to the practice of ritual magic or the *Ars Goetia*</note>. If this Paimon speaks in a way that the conjurer does not understand, let the conjurer not be dismayed. But once he has delivered his first bond <note>original: "obligation," referring to a magical contract or oath of obedience</note> to fulfill the conjurer's desire, the conjurer must also command him to answer distinctly and plainly all questions asked regarding philosophy, wisdom, science, and all other secret things. If you wish to know the nature of the world—what the earth is, what holds it up in the water, what the Abyss <note>original: *Abyssus*</note> is, or where the wind is and from where it comes—he will teach you abundantly. He can also explain consecrations and sacrifices, as well as other rituals. He grants titles and confirmations of status; he binds those who resist him with his own chains and subjects them to the conjurer; he provides good familiar spirits and possesses an understanding of all arts.

<margin>Cautions for the Exorcist or Conjurer.</margin>
Note that when calling him up, the exorcist must look toward the Northwest, because that is where his home is. When he is summoned, let the exorcist receive him steadfastly without fear. Let him ask whatever questions or demands he pleases, and no doubt he shall obtain the same from him. The exorcist must take care not to forget the Creator because of the wonders previously described regarding Paimon. Some say he belongs to the order of **Dominions**; others say he is of the order of **Cherubim**. He is followed by two hundred legions, partly from the order of **Angels** and partly from the **Powers** <note>original: *Potestates*</note>. Note that if Paimon is summoned alone by an offering or sacrifice, two kings follow him—namely **Bebal** and **Abalam**—along with other potentates. In his host are twenty-five legions, because the spirits subject to them are not always with them unless they are compelled to appear by divine power.

<margin>The fall of Belial.</margin>
Some say that King **Belial** was created immediately after **Lucifer**, and therefore they believe he was the father and seducer of those who fell from the heavenly orders. He was among the first to fall from the nobler and wiser sort, who ranked higher than **Michael** and the other heavenly angels who remained. Although Belial preceded all those who were thrown down to the earth, he did not precede those who stayed in heaven. This Belial is forced by divine power to give true answers to those who offer sacrifices, gifts, and offerings. However, he does not remain truthful for even an hour unless he is constrained by divine power, as previously mentioned. He takes the form of a beautiful angel sitting in a fiery chariot. He speaks elegantly and distributes senatorial appointments, the favor of friends, and excellent familiar spirits. He rules over eighty legions, partly from the order of **Virtues** and partly from the order of **Angels**. He is sometimes found in the form of an exorcist within the "bond of spirits" <note>a ritual constraint used to bind demons</note>. The exorcist must consider that Belial assists his subjects in everything. If he will not submit himself, let the "bond of spirits" be read. 

<margin>Solomon gathered all the devils together in a brass vessel.</margin>
The spirits' chain is sent for him, with which the wise **Solomon** gathered them together with their legions in a brass <note>original: "brasen"</note> vessel. Enclosed within that vessel among all the legions were seventy-two kings, the chief of whom was **Biloth**, the second was **Belial**, the third was **Asmoday**, and over a million <note>original: "thousand thousand"</note> legions. Without doubt, I must confess I learned this from my master Solomon; however, he did not tell me why he gathered them together and shut them up in that way, but I believe it was because of Belial’s pride. Certain necromancers <note>original: "Negromancers"</note> say that Solomon was one day seduced by the craft of a certain woman and was persuaded to pray before this same idol, named Belial, but this is not credible. Therefore, we should rather believe (as previously stated) that they were gathered together in that great brass vessel for their pride and arrogance and thrown into a deep lake or hole in **Babylon**. For wise Solomon performed his deeds through Divine power, which...

But this Belial entered into a certain idol and gave answers to those who offered sacrifices to him, as **Toex** <note>possibly a reference to Michael Toxites, a 16th-century physician and editor of Paracelsus</note> reports in his writings; and so the Babylonians worshipped and sacrificed to him.

<margin>Bune.</margin> **Bune** is a great and strong Duke. He appears as a dragon with three heads, the third of which is like a man. He speaks with a divine voice; he makes the dead move from their places and causes devils to assemble upon the tombs of the dead. He greatly enriches a person and makes them eloquent and wise, answering truly to all demands. Thirty legions obey him.

<margin>Forneus.</margin> **Forneus** is a great Marquess, resembling a monster of the sea. He makes men wonderful in rhetoric; he provides a person with a good reputation and the knowledge of languages, and makes one beloved by both foes and friends. There are under him twenty-nine legions, belonging partly to the order of Thrones and partly to the order of Angels.

<margin>Ronove.</margin> **Ronove** is a Marquess and an Earl. He resembles a monster. He brings extraordinary understanding in rhetoric, faithful servants, knowledge of languages, and the favor of both friends and foes. Nineteen legions obey him.

<margin>Berith, a golden devil.</margin> **Berith** is a great and terrible Duke and has three names: some call him **Beal**, the Jews call him **Berith**, and necromancers <note>magicians who communicate with the dead or spirits</note> call him **Bolfry**. He appears as a red soldier in red clothing, riding a horse of that same color, with a crown on his head. He answers truly regarding things present, past, and to come. He is compelled at a certain hour through divine power by a ring used in the magical art. He is also a liar; he turns all metals into gold; he bestows dignities <note>titles or high offices</note> and confirms them. He speaks with a clear and subtle voice, and twenty-six legions are under him.

<margin>Astaroth.</margin> **Astaroth** is a great and strong Duke, appearing in the shape of a foul angel, sitting upon an infernal dragon and carrying a viper in his right hand. He answers truly regarding matters present, past, and to come, and also concerning all secrets. He talks willingly about the creator of spirits and their fall—how they sinned and fell. He claims he did not fall of his own accord. He makes a person wonderfully learned in the liberal arts <note>original: "Liberal Sciences"</note> and rules forty legions. Every exorcist must take heed not to let him come too near, because of his stinking breath. Therefore, the conjurer should hold a magical ring near his face, which shall defend him.

<margin>Foras.</margin> **Foras** (also known as **Forcas**) is a great President and is seen in the form of a strong man. In human shape, he understands the properties of herbs and precious stones. He teaches logic and ethics in full, as well as their various branches. He makes a man invisible, clever, eloquent, and long-lived. He recovers lost things, discovers treasures, and is Lord over twenty-nine legions.

<margin>Furfur.</margin> **Furfur** is a great Earl, appearing as a stag with a fiery tail. He lies about everything unless he is brought within a magical triangle <note>a geometric figure used in ritual magic to contain a spirit and force it to tell the truth</note>. When commanded, he takes on an angelic form. He speaks with a hoarse voice and willingly creates love between a husband and wife. He raises thunder, lightning, and windstorms. When commanded, he answers well regarding both secret and divine things, and he has rule and dominion over twenty-six legions.

<margin>Marchosias.</margin> **Marchosias** is a great Marquess. He shows himself in the shape of a cruel wolf with the wings of a griffin, a serpent's tail, and spitting something indefinable out of his mouth. When he is in human shape, he is an excellent fighter. He answers all questions truly and is faithful in all the conjurer's business. He was originally of the order of Dominions <note>original: "Dominations," a high rank in the celestial hierarchy</note>. Under him are thirty legions. He hopes to return to the seventh throne after 1,200 years, but he is deceived in that hope.

# BOOK XV. The Discovery of Devils and Spirits.

<margin>Malphas.</margin>
**Malphas** is a great President. He appears in the form of a crow, but when clothed in human form, he speaks with a hoarse voice. He builds houses and high towers wonderfully and quickly gathers craftsmen <note>original: "Artificers"</note> together. He also throws down the buildings <note>original: "edifications"</note> of enemies. He helps provide good familiar spirits and willingly receives sacrifices, though he deceives all those who perform the sacrifices. Forty legions obey him.

<margin>Vepar.</margin>
**Vepar** (also known as **Separ**) is a great and strong Duke. He resembles a mermaid <note>In this context, the term is used for a sea-dwelling spirit, often depicted as a merman elsewhere</note>. He is the guide of the waters and of ships laden with weapons <note>original: "armour"</note>. At the command of his master, he causes the sea to become rough and stormy and makes it appear full of phantom ships. He kills men within three days by causing their wounds to rot and fill with maggots; however, these wounds can be healed with proper care. He rules twenty-nine legions.

<margin>Sabnack.</margin>
**Sabnack** (also known as **Salmack**) is a great and strong Marquess. He comes forth as an armed soldier with a lion’s head, riding on a pale horse. He marvelously changes a person's appearance and features <note>original: "form and favour"</note>. He builds high towers full of weapons, as well as castles and cities. For thirty days, he afflicts men with wounds that are both rotten and full of maggots. At the command of the exorcist, he provides good familiar spirits and has dominion over fifty legions.

<margin>Sidonay.</margin>
**Sidonay** (also known as **Asmoday**) is a great, strong, and mighty King. He is seen with three heads: the first is like a bull, the second like a man, and the third like a ram. He has a serpent’s tail and breathes flames out of his mouth. He has feet like a goose and sits upon an infernal dragon, carrying a lance and a banner in his hand. He precedes others who are under the power of **Amaymon**. When the conjurer performs this ritual <note>original: "exerciseth this office"</note>, he should be outdoors, wary, and standing on his feet. If his cap remains on his head, Asmoday will cause all his actions to be betrayed <note>original: "bewrayed"</note>; if he does not follow these precautions, the exorcist will be deceived by Amaymon in everything. But as soon as the exorcist sees him in the form described above, he must call him by his name, saying, "You are Asmoday." The spirit will not deny it and will immediately bow down to the ground. He gives the "ring of virtues" and perfectly teaches geometry, arithmetic, astronomy, and handicrafts. He answers all questions fully and truly, makes a person invisible, and shows the places where treasure is hidden (guarding it if it is among the legions of Amaymon). He has seventy-two legions under his power.

<margin>Gaap.</margin>
<margin>Who was the first Necromancer.</margin>
**Gaap** (also known as **Tap**) is a great President and a Prince. He appears under a southern <note>original: "meridional"</note> sign, and when he takes human shape, he is the guide of the four principal kings and is as mighty as **Bileth**. There were certain necromancers who offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to him; to summon him, they practiced a ritual <note>original: "art"</note> they claimed was created by the wise King Solomon, but this is false. It was actually **Ham** <note>original: "Cham"</note>, the son of Noah, who first began to call upon <note>original: "invocate"</note> wicked spirits after the Great Flood. He summoned Bileth and created a ritual in his name, as well as a book known to many astrologers <note>original: "Mathematicians," which in the 16th century often referred to those who calculated horoscopes or occult charts</note>. Burnt offerings and sacrifices were made, and gifts were given, and much wickedness was performed by the exorcist, who mixed the holy names of God throughout the ritual. Indeed <note>original: "Marry"</note>, there is a letter <note>original: "Epistle"</note> regarding those names written by Solomon, as recorded by **Elias of Jerusalem** <note>original: "Helias Hierofolymitanus"</note> and **Helifam**. It should be noted that if any exorcist possesses the ritual of Bileth but cannot make him appear or stand before him, I must not reveal <note>original: "bewray"</note> how to constrain him, because it is an abomination, and because I have learned nothing from Solomon regarding his rank and office. However, I will not hide this: he makes a man wonderful in philosophy and all the liberal sciences. He causes love, hatred, and insensibility. He handles the consecration of things belonging to the dominion of Amaymon and rescues familiar spirits from the possession of other conjurers. He answers truly and perfectly regarding things present, past, and future, and transports men very quickly to other nations. He rules sixty-six legions and was originally of the Order of Powers <note>original: "Potestates," one of the traditional nine choirs of angels</note>.

**Shax** (also known as **Scox**) is a dark and great Marquess. He looks like a stork and has a hoarse, thin <note>original: "subtil"</note> voice. He marvelously takes away the sight, hearing, and understanding...

# Sidonay. Of Witchcraft. CHAPTER 11.

[Sidonay] ...standing of any man, at the commandment of the conjuror. He takes away money out of every king's house and carries it back after 1,200 years if he is commanded. He is a horse-stealer and is thought to be faithful in all commandments; and although he promises to be obedient to the conjuror in all things, he is not actually so. He is a liar, except when he is brought into a triangle; there, he speaks divinely and tells of things that are hidden and not guarded by wicked spirits. He promises good familiar spirits, which are accepted if they are not deceivers. He has thirty legions.

<margin>Procel</margin>
**Procel** is a great and strong Duke, appearing in the shape of an angel, but he speaks darkly of hidden things. He teaches geometry and the liberal arts. He makes great noises and causes waters to roar where there are none. He warms waters and tempers baths at certain times, as the exorcist appoints him. He was of the Order of Powers <note>original: "Potestates," the sixth of the nine celestial orders of angels</note> and has forty-eight legions under his power.

<margin>Furcas</margin>
**Furcas** is a knight and comes forth in the likeness of a cruel man with a long beard and a gray <note>original: "hoary"</note> head. He sits on a pale horse, carrying a sharp weapon in his hand. He perfectly teaches practical philosophy, rhetoric, logic, astronomy, chiromancy <note>original: "Chiromancy," the art of palm reading</note>, pyromancy <note>original: "Pyromancy," divination by observing fire</note>, and their various parts. Twenty legions obey him.

<margin>Murmur</margin>
**Murmur** is a great Duke and an Earl, appearing in the shape of a soldier riding on a griffin, with a duke's crown on his head. Two of his ministers go before him with great trumpets. He teaches philosophy completely <note>original: "absolutely"</note> and constrains souls to appear before the exorcist to answer whatever he asks them. He was partly of the Order of Thrones and partly of the Order of Angels, and he rules thirty legions.

<margin>Caim</margin>
**Caim** is a great President, taking the form of a thrush; but when he puts on a man’s shape, he answers from within burning ashes, carrying a most sharp sword in his hand. He makes the best debaters <note>original: "disputers"</note> and gives men the understanding of all birds, the lowing of bullocks, the barking of dogs, and also the sound and noise of waters. He gives the best answers regarding things to come. He was of the Order of Angels and rules thirty legions.

<margin>Raum</margin>
**Raum** (or **Raim**) is a great Earl. He is seen as a crow, but when he puts on human shape at the commandment of the exorcist, he steals wonderfully out of the king's house and carries the theft wherever he is assigned. He destroys cities and has great contempt for honors and titles <note>original: "dignities"</note>. He knows things present, past, and to come, and reconciles friends and foes. He was of the Order of Thrones and governs thirty legions.

<margin>Halphas</margin>
**Halphas** is a great Earl and comes abroad like a stork with a hoarse voice. He notably builds up towns full of ammunition and weapons; he sends men of war to appointed places and has twenty-six legions under him.

<margin>Focalor</margin>
**Focalor** is a great Duke who comes forth as a man with wings like a griffin. He kills men and drowns them in the waters, and he overturns ships of war, commanding and ruling both winds and seas. The conjuror should note that if he bids Focalor to hurt no man, the spirit willingly consents. He hopes to return to the Seventh Throne after 1,000 years, but he is deceived. He has three legions.

<margin>Vine</margin>
**Vine** is a great King and an Earl. He shows himself as a lion riding a black horse and carries a viper in his hand. He gladly builds large towers, throws down stone walls, and makes waters rough. At the commandment of the exorcist, he answers regarding hidden things, witches, and things present, past, and to come.

<margin>Bifrons</margin>
**Bifrons** is seen in the likeness of a monster when he takes the image of a man. He makes one wonderfully cunning in astrology, completely explaining the mansions of the planets. He does the like in geometry and other measurements. He perfectly understands the strength and virtue of herbs, precious stones, and woods. He moves dead bodies from place to place and appears to light candles upon the graves <note>original: "sepulchres"</note> of the dead. He has twenty-six legions under him.

### Book XV. The Discovery of Devils and Spirits.

<margin>Gamigin.</margin> **Gamigin** is a great Marquess and is seen in the form of a little horse. When he takes human shape, he speaks with a hoarse voice, debating all the Liberal Sciences <note>The "Liberal Sciences" or "Liberal Arts" traditionally included grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.</note>. He also brings it to pass that the souls who were drowned in the sea, or those who dwell in Purgatory (which is called *Cartagra*, that is, the "affliction of souls") shall take on airy bodies and visibly appear and answer questions at the conjurer’s command. He remains with the exorcist until he has accomplished his desires, and he has thirty legions under him.

<margin>Zagan.</margin> **Zagan** is a great King and a President. He comes forth like a bull with griffin's wings; but when he takes human shape, he makes men witty. He turns all metals into the coin of that territory and turns water into wine, and wine into water. He also turns blood into wine, and wine into blood, and a fool into a wise man. He is the head of thirty-three legions.

<margin>Orias.</margin> **Orias** is a great Marquess and is seen as a lion riding on a strong horse with a serpent's tail; he carries two great hissing serpents in his right hand. He knows the positions <note>original: "mansions"</note> of the planets and perfectly teaches the virtues of the stars. He transforms men and grants dignities, high church offices <note>original: "Prelacies"</note>, and official confirmations, as well as the favor of both friends and foes. He has thirty legions under him.

<margin>Valac.</margin> **Valac** is a great President and comes forth with angel's wings like a boy riding on a two-headed dragon. He answers perfectly regarding hidden treasures and where serpents may be seen, which he delivers into the conjurer's hands deprived of any force or strength. He has dominion over thirty legions of devils.

<margin>Gemory.</margin> **Gemory** is a strong and mighty Duke. He appears like a beautiful woman with a duchess’s coronet tied around her waist, riding on a camel. He answers well and truly of things present, past, and to come, and of hidden treasure and where it lies. He procures the love of women, especially of young maids, and has twenty-six legions.

<margin>Decarabia.</margin> **Decarabia** (or **Carabia**) comes in the form of a star <note>The original text uses a star symbol (*)</note>. He has thirty legions.

<margin>Amduscias.</margin> **Amduscias** is a great and strong Duke. He comes forth as a unicorn. When he stands before his master in human shape at his command, he easily brings it to pass that trumpets and all musical instruments may be heard but not seen; he also causes trees to bend and lean according to the conjurer's will. He is excellent among familiar spirits and has twenty-nine legions.

<margin>Andras.</margin> **Andras** is a great Marquess and is seen in an angel's shape, with a head like a black night-raven, riding upon a black and very strong wolf, flourishing a sharp sword in his hand. He can kill the master, the servant, and all assistants. He is the author of discords and rules thirty legions.

<margin>Andrealphus.</margin> **Andrealphus** is a great Marquess appearing as a peacock. He makes a man into a subtle debater and cunning in astronomy, and he transforms a man into the likeness of a bird. There are thirty legions under him.

<margin>Ose.</margin> **Ose** is a great President and comes forth like a leopard. When pretending to be a man, he makes one skilled in the Liberal Sciences. He answers truly regarding divine and secret things. He transforms a man's shape and brings a man to such madness that he thinks himself to be that which he is not—such as one who thinks he is a King or a Pope, or that he wears a crown on his head. *And that kingdom lasts for an hour* <note>original: "Duratq; id regnum ad horam."</note>.

<margin>Aym.</margin> **Aym** (or **Haborim**) is a great and strong Duke. He rides on a viper, carrying a lit firebrand in his hand, with the flame of which castles and cities are set on fire. He makes one witty in every kind of way; he answers truly regarding private matters and reigns over twenty-six legions.

# The Same. Of Witchcraft. CHAPTER 11. <note>original: "Iidem," Latin for "The same," referring to the continued list of spirits.</note>

<margin>Orobas.</margin> **Orobas** is a great Prince. He comes forth in the form of a horse, but when he takes on a man's form <note>original: "idol," meaning an image or physical representation</note>, he speaks of divine virtue. He gives true answers regarding things present, past, and to come, and concerning divinity and the creation. He deceives no one, nor does he allow anyone to be tempted. He bestows dignities and high church offices <note>original: "prelacies"</note>, as well as the favor of both friends and foes; he has rule over twenty legions.

<margin>Cimeries.</margin> **Cimeries** is a great and powerful Marquess, ruling in the parts of Africa. He teaches grammar, logic, and rhetoric perfectly. He discovers treasures and hidden things. He brings it to pass that a man shall seem to be quickly <note>original: "with expedition"</note> transformed into a soldier. He rides upon a great black horse and rules twenty legions.

He hopes to return to the seventh throne after one thousand two hundred years—though this is not credible.

He gladly talks of divinity, the creation of the world, and the Fall. He is constrained by divine power <note>original: "vertue"</note>—as are all devils and spirits—to burn and destroy all the conjurer's adversaries. He makes men invisible and wise. He governs forty legions and was formerly of the order of Dominions <note>another rank in the traditional hierarchy of angels</note>.

<margin>Allocer.</margin> **Allocer** is a powerful and great Duke. He comes forth like a soldier riding on a great horse. He has a lion's face, very red, with flaming eyes. <margin>Saleos.</margin> **Saleos** is a great Earl. He appears as a gallant soldier riding on a crocodile and wears a Duke's crown; he is peaceable, and so forth.

<margin>Vuall.</margin> **Vuall** is a great and powerful Duke. He was of the order of Powers <note>original: "Potestates"</note> and governs thirty-seven legions.

<margin>Haagenti.</margin> **Haagenti** is a great President, appearing like a great bull with the wings of a griffin. However, when he takes human shape, he makes a man wise in everything. <margin>Phœnix.</margin> **Phœnix** is a great Marquess, appearing like the bird Phoenix and having a child’s voice. But before he stands still before the conjurer, he sings many sweet notes. Then the exorcist, with his companions, must beware not to listen to the melody, but must immediately <note>original: "by and by"</note> bid him take on human shape. Then he will speak marvelously of all wonderful sciences. He is an excellent and obedient poet. He hopes to return to the seventh throne after one thousand two hundred years and governs twenty legions.

### CHAPTER 12.

->The hours during which the principal devils may be bound—that is, summoned and restrained from doing harm.<-

<margin>This was the work of someone named T. R., written in beautiful red and black letters on parchment and created by him in the year 1570. He claimed it was for the support of his livelihood, the education of the poor, and the glory of God’s holy name.</margin>**Amaymon** (King of the East), **Corson** (King of the South), **Zimimar** (King of the North), and **Goap** (King and Prince of the West) may be bound from 9:00 AM <note>original: "the third hour"</note> until noon, and from 3:00 PM <note>original: "the ninth hour"</note> until evening. 

**Marquesses** may be bound from 3:00 PM <note>original: "the ninth hour"</note> until the time of night prayer <note>original: "compline," the final church service of the day</note>, and from then until the end of the day. 

**Dukes** may be bound from 6:00 AM <note>original: "the first hour"</note> until noon; clear weather must be observed for this. 

**Prelates** may be bound at any hour of the day. 

**Knights** may be bound from dawn until sunrise, or from the time of evening prayer <note>original: "evensong"</note> until sunset. 

A **President** may not be bound at any hour of the day unless the King whom he obeys is also invoked, nor can he be bound at nightfall. 

**Counts** or **Earls** may be bound at any hour of the day, provided it is in the woods or fields where people do not usually go.

### CHAPTER 13.

->The method of adjuring <term>adjuring: commanding or summoning a spirit through a formal oath or ritual</term> or summoning the aforementioned spirits to appear.<-

When you wish to summon any spirit, you must know his name and his office. You must also fast and remain pure from all physical "pollution" for three or four days beforehand; this will make the spirit more obedient to you. Then, draw a ritual circle and call up the spirit with great focus. While holding a ritual ring in your hand, recite this prayer following in your own name and the name of your companion (for you must always have one person with you). If you do this, no spirit shall bother you, and your purpose will succeed. Note how closely this agrees with Catholic <note>original: "Popish"</note> charms and conjurations.

> *In the Name of our Lord Jesus Christ, the ✠ Father, ✠ the Son, ✠ and the Holy Ghost ✠—Holy Trinity and unspeakable Unity—I call upon you, that you may be my salvation and defense, and the protection of my body and soul, and of all my goods. Through the power of your Holy Cross, and through the power of your passion, I beseech you, O Lord Jesus Christ, by the merits of your blessed Mother Saint Mary, and of all your Saints, that you give me Grace and Divine power over all the wicked spirits. Whichever of them I call by name, let them come immediately from every region and fulfill my will, so that they are neither hurtful nor frightening to me, but rather obedient and helpful to me. And through your power strictly commanding them, let them fulfill my commandments. Amen.*

# THE DISCOVERY OF WITCHCRAFT. CHAPTER 13.

<margin>Note the names attributed to Christ by the conjurer in this ritual of exorcism.</margin>
Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of *Sabbaoth* <note>original: "Sabbaoth," a Hebrew term meaning "of hosts" or "of armies"</note>, who will come to judge the living <note>original: "quick"</note> and the dead; you who are Alpha and Omega, the first and the last, King of Kings, and Lord of Lords: *Ioth*, *Aglanabzath*, *El*, *Abiel*, *Anathiel*, *Amazim*, *Sedomel*, *Gayes*, *Heli*, *Messias*, *Tolimi*, *Elias*, *Ischiros*, *Athanatos*, *Imas*. By these, your holy names, and by all others, I call upon you and beg you, O Lord Jesus Christ—by your birth and baptism, by your cross and passion, by your ascension, and by the coming of the Holy Spirit; by the bitterness of your soul when it departed from the body, by your five wounds, by the blood and water which came out of your body, by your power, by the Sacrament which you gave your disciples the day before you suffered, by the holy Trinity and the inseparable Unity, by blessed Mary your mother, by your angels, archangels, prophets, patriarchs, and by all your saints, and by all the sacraments which are made in your honor—I worship and beg you to accept these prayers, conjurations, and words of my mouth, which I will use. I require of you, O Lord Jesus Christ, that you give me your power and authority over all your angels (which were thrown down from heaven to deceive mankind) to draw them to me, to tie and bind them, and also to release <note>original: "loose"</note> them; to gather them together before me, and to command them to do all that they can, and that by no means they should despise my voice or the words of my mouth, but that they obey me and my sayings, and fear me. I beg you by your humanity, mercy, and grace; and I require of you *Adonai* <note>original: "Adony"</note>, *Amay*, *Hozta*, *Vegedoza*, *Mitai*, *Hel*, *Suranat*, *Psion*, *Plesy*, and by all your holy names, and by all your holy male and female saints, by all your angels and archangels, powers, dominions, and virtues, and by that name with which Solomon bound the devils and shut them up—*Elbzach*, *Ebanher*, *Agle*, *Goth*, *Ioth*, *Othie*, *Venoch*, *Nabzat*—and by all your holy names which are written in this book, and by the power of them all: that you enable me to gather all your spirits thrown down from heaven, so that they may give me a true answer to all my demands, and that they satisfy all my requests, without hurting my body or soul, or anything else that is mine, through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, forever and ever <note>original: "world without end"</note>.

<margin>What wonderful power conjurers believe exists in these forged names of Christ.</margin>
Oh Father Almighty, oh wise Son, oh Holy Spirit, the searcher of hearts; oh you three persons, one true Godhead in substance, who spared Adam and Eve in their sins; and oh you, the Son, who died for their sins a most shameful <note>original: "filthy," meaning base or degrading</note> death, enduring it upon the holy cross; oh you most merciful, when I fly to your mercy and beg you by all the means I can, by these holy names of your Son—namely, Alpha and Omega and all his other names—grant me your power and strength, that I may be able to summon <note>original: "cite"</note> before me your spirits which were thrown down from heaven, and that they may speak with me, and act immediately without delay, and with a good will, and without the hurt of my body, soul, or goods, etc., as is contained in the book called *The Ring of Solomon* <note>original: "Annulus Solomonis"</note>.

Oh great and eternal power of the highest, which through your will <note>original: "disposition"</note>, these being called to judgment: *Wachoon*, *Stumulamaton*, *Esphares*, *Tetragrammaton* <note>the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, *Oliozam*, *Cryon*, *Epytion*, *Erition*, *Eriona*, *Onela*, *Bzafim*, *Nopm*, *Messias*, *Soter* <note>Greek for "Savior"</note>, *Emanuel*, *Sabboth*, *Adonay*. I worship you, I call upon you, I implore you with all the strength of my mind, that by you, my present prayers, consecrations, and conjurations be hallowed; and wherever wicked spirits are called in the power of your names, they may come together from every region <note>original: "coast"</note> and diligently fulfill my will as the exorcist. Let it be done, let it be done, let it be done; Amen <note>original: "Fiat, fiat, fiat; Amen"</note>.

...his neck, from his back, from his breast, from his nipples <note>original: "paps"</note>, from his heart, from his stomach, from his sides, from his flesh, from his blood, from his bones, from his legs, from his feet, from his fingers, from the soles of his feet, from his marrow, from his sinews, from his skin, and from every joint of his limbs <note>original: "members"</note>, etc.

Doubtless Jesus Christ could have no hiding place <note>original: "startling hole"</note>, but was hereby prevented and pursued in every way; so much so that he was forced to perform the cure. For it appears from this that it would have been insufficient for him to have said, "Depart out of this man, you unclean spirit," and that when he said so, he did not actually perform it. I do not think that there will be found among all the heathen superstitious fables, or among the witches, conjurers, poets, knaves, swindlers <note>original: "coseners"</note>, fools, etc., that ever wrote, so impudent and impious a lie or charm as is read in Bernardino de' Busti <note>original: "Barnardine de busis"</note>. There, to cure a sick man, Christ's body—specifically, a communion wafer <note>original: "Wafer-cake"</note>—was applied outwardly to his side and entered into his heart in the sight of all bystanders. Now, if serious authors report such lies, what credit should we give to the old wives' tales that Sprenger, Institor <note>Heinrich Kramer (Institoris) and Jacob Sprenger were the authors of the *Malleus Maleficarum*, the most famous medieval treatise on witch-hunting.</note>, Bodin, and others write? We should give them as much credit as we give to *Ovid's Metamorphoses*, *Aesop's Fables*, *More's Utopia*, and various other fantasies, which have as much truth in them as a blind man has sight in his eye.

->A Charm for the Bots <term>Bots are parasitic larvae that infest the stomachs of horses.</term> in a Horse.<-

You must both say and do this to the diseased horse for three days together, before sunrise: "In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit <note>original: "In Nomine Patris & filii & Spiritus sancti"</note>; I exorcise you, worm, by God the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit <note>original: "Exorcizo te vermem per Deum Patrem, & filium & Spiritum sanctum"</note>: In the Name of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, I conjure you, O Worm, by God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, that you neither eat nor drink the flesh, blood, or bones of this horse; and that you may hereby be made as patient as Job, and as good as Saint John the Baptist when he baptized Christ in the Jordan. In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit <note>original: "In Nomine Patris & Filii & Spiritus Sancti"</note>." And then say three *Pater Nosters* <term>The Lord's Prayer ("Our Father").</term> and three *Aves* <term>The "Hail Mary" prayer.</term> in the right ear of the horse, to the glory of the Holy Trinity. "The Lord, the Son, and the Spirit of Mary" <note>original: "Dominus Filius & Spiritus Mariae"</note>.
<margin>Blacksmiths will give them little thanks for this prayer.</margin>
There are also various books printed, as it would appear, with the authority of the Church of Rome, which contain many medicinal prayers. These are not only for all diseases of horses, but also for every hindrance and fault in a horse; in so much that if a shoe falls off in the middle of a journey, there is a prayer to protect your horse's hoof so that it will not break, no matter how far he is from the blacksmith's forge.
Likewise, the Duke of Alba's horse was consecrated or canonized in the Low Countries <note>The coastal region of northwestern Europe, including the modern-day Netherlands and Belgium.</note> at a solemn Mass. During this, the Pope's Bull and also his charm were published (which I will recite later). Meanwhile, the Duke sat as Viceroy with his consecrated standard in his hand until the Mass was finished.

->A Charm against Vinegar.<-

<margin>O notable blasphemy!</margin>
To ensure that wine does not turn sour <note>original: "wax eager"</note>, write on the vessel: "Taste and see, for the Lord is sweet" <note>original: "Gustate & videte, quoniam suavis est Dominus"</note>.

### Chapter 15

*The Enchanting of Serpents and Snakes; objections answered concerning the reasons why charms take effect on them. Muhammad's Pigeon. A miracle performed by an ass at Memphis in Egypt. Popish charms against serpents. Of miracle-workers, the taming of snakes, and Bodin's lie about snakes.* <note>Jean Bodin (1530–1596) was a French jurist and writer on demonology whom Scot frequently critiques for his belief in witchcraft.</note>

Concerning the charming of serpents and snakes, my adversaries (as I have said) think they have a great advantage by the words of David in <margin>Psalm 58 and Jeremiah 8, interpreting one Prophet by Virgil and the other by Ovid.</margin> For the words of David are these: *Their poison is like the poison of a serpent, and like a deaf adder that stops its ear and the voice of the charmer, charm he never so cunningly.* <margin>Psalm 58:4, 5</margin> The words of Virgil are these: *The cold snake in the meadows is burst by singing.* <margin>Virgil, Eclogues 8. Original: "Frigidus in pratis cantando rumpitur anguis."</margin> This is as if to say, "David, you lie"; for the cold-natured snake is broken all to pieces in the field where it lies by the charms of the enchanters. Then comes Ovid, and he speaks in the name and person of a witch: *I break the viper’s jaws with words and spells.* <margin>Ovid, Metamorphoses 7. Original: "Vipereas rumpo verbis & carmine fauces."</margin> Indeed, Jeremiah on the other side encounters this poetical witch, and he not only defends but explains his fellow prophet’s words—and that not in his own name, but in the name of Almighty God, saying: *I will send serpents and cockatrices <term>A mythical serpent, also called a basilisk, said to kill with its breath or glance.</term> among you which cannot be charmed.* <margin>Jeremiah 8:17</margin>

Now let any impartial man (Christian or Heathen) judge whether the words and minds of the Prophets do not directly oppose <term>original: "oppugn"</term> these poets' words. I am sure that in this they did but jest and trifle, according to the common fables of lying poets. And certainly, I can counter them with two other poets, namely Propertius and Horace, the one merrily mocking and the other seriously opposing their fantastical poetry concerning the power and omnipotence of witches. For where Virgil, Ovid, etc., write that witches with their charms fetch down the moon and stars from heaven, Propertius mocks them in the following words:

->But you who have the trick of drawing down the Moon,<-
->And labor to prepare sacred things with magic deceptions,<-
->Come then, change our mistress's mind,<-
->And make her face more pale than mine:<-
->Then I would believe that you could lead down both stars and rivers<-
->By the spells of Circe.<-
<note>original Latin: "At vos deductæ quibus est fallacia Lunæ, / Et labor in magicis sacra parare fucis, / En agedum dominæ mentem convertite nostræ, / Et facite illa meo palleat ore magis, / Tunc ego crediderim vobis & sidera & amnes / Posse Circeis ducere carminibus."</note>

->Translated into English by Abraham Fleming:<-

->But you that have the subtle sleight<-

### *The Aspects of the Planets*

☌ <term>Conjunction</term> is the best alignment with beneficial planets, and the worst with harmful ones.
✱ <term>Sextile</term> is an average alignment in terms of goodness or badness.
△ <term>Trine</term> is very beneficial when aligned with good planets, and does not cause harm even with evil ones.
□ <term>Square</term>: This alignment represents an incomplete hostility.
☍ <term>Opposition</term>: This alignment represents a complete and perfect hostility.

### *How the Day is divided or distinguished*

A natural day <note>original: "Day natural"</note> is the span of twenty-four hours, including the night, and begins at one o'clock after midnight.
An artificial day is the span of time between the rising and the setting <note>original: "falling"</note> of the sun, and so on; all the rest is night, and it begins at sunrise.

Below follows a table showing how the day and the night are divided by hours and assigned to the rule <note>original: "regiment"</note> of the planets.

# Book XII. The Discovery of Charms, etc.

...against Vipers, allowed for the most part in and by the Church of Rome, as follows:

<margin>Exorcisms or Conjurations against Serpents.</margin>
I conjure you, O Serpent, in this hour, by the five holy wounds of our Lord, that you do not move from this place, but stay here as certainly as God was born of a pure Virgin. Otherwise, I conjure you, Serpent, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit <note>original: "In Nomine Patris, & Filii, & Spiritus Sancti"</note>: I command you, Serpent, by our Lady Saint Mary, that you obey me as wax obeys fire, and as fire obeys water; that you hurt neither me nor any other Christian, as certainly as God was born of an immaculate Virgin, in which respect I take you up, In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. *Ely lash eiter, ely lash eiter.* Otherwise, O Vermin, you must come as God came to the Jews. Otherwise, L. Varius says that a serpent shrunk by oak leaves <note>original: "Serpens quernis frondibus contracta"</note>—that is, a serpent touched with oak leaves—dies, and stops even at the beginning of its movement if a feather of the *Ibis* bird is cast or thrown upon it. He also says that a Viper hit with a reed is stunned, and if touched with a beech branch, it is presently numbed and stiff.

<margin>L. Vair. book on fascination, chapter 4.</margin>
Here it should be remembered that many people boast they are of Saint Paul's race and kindred, showing marks of serpents upon their bodies. The Papists <note>A term used by the author for followers of the Roman Catholic Church.</note> affirm this was common to all those of Saint Paul’s stock. Indeed, they say along with this that all his relatives can handle serpents or any poison without danger. Others likewise brag they have a "Catherine-wheel" mark upon their bodies; they say they are kin to Saint Catherine, and that they can carry burning coals in their bare hands, dip their hands in hot scalding liquid, and even go into hot ovens. 

<margin>Usurpers of kinship with blessed Paul and Saint Catherine.</margin>
Regarding these claims: though the last one (entering ovens) is just a simple jest that can be done by anyone who tries it—as a rogue in London used to do, by not staying inside for any length of time—there is a display made of the others as if they were certain and undoubted. This is done by anointing the hands with the juice of mallows, mercury, urine, etc., which for a short time act as <term>defensatives</term> <note>original: "defensatives"; substances used to protect the skin from heat.</note> against scalding liquids and scorching fires.

But those who take it upon themselves to perform these mysteries and miracles do indeed—after reciting these and similar words and charms—take up snakes and vipers in their bare hands. Sometimes they even put them around their necks without receiving any hurt, to the terror and astonishment of the beholders, who naturally both fear and abhor all serpents. But these charmers (take my word for it) dare not trust their charms. Instead, they use a type of enchantment that any man may lawfully use, and the lawful use of it ensures they shall be safe and take no harm, no matter how much they handle them. Truly, as some men say, they pull out the snakes' teeth beforehand with a woolen rag; but the truth is, they weary the snakes out, and that is a certainty. Surely this is a kind of witchcraft which I call <term>private confederacy</term> <note>A secret arrangement or trick rather than actual magic.</note>. Bodin says that all the snakes in one country were driven into another region by charms and verses; perhaps he means Ireland, where Saint Patrick is said to have done this by his holiness, etc.

<margin>J. Bodin, book on demons, book 1, chapter 3.</margin>
James Sprenger and Henry Institor <note>original: "Institoris"; the authors of the "Malleus Maleficarum," a famous witch-hunting manual.</note> affirm that serpents, snakes, and their skins exceed all other creatures for use in witchcraft. They claim witches commonly bury them under men's thresholds, either of the house or the cattle stalls, to cause barrenness in both women and beasts. They even claim that the very earth and ashes of these snakes continue to have the power of <term>fascination</term> <note>The power to cast a spell or "evil eye" through a look or presence.</note>. Because of this, they advise everyone to occasionally dig away the earth under their thresholds and sprinkle holy water in that place. They also suggest hanging boughs—hallowed on Midsummer Day—at the stall door where the cattle stand. They produce examples of witchcraft to support this, or perhaps their own stories, which I will omit because I see my book is growing larger than I intended it to be.

Let the Master and his companion sit down in their circle, the Master holding the book in his hand and his companion holding the crystal stone in his right hand, looking into the stone when the fairy appears. But regarding these wax images, it is certain that they are much feared among the people and frequently used by deceitful <term>cousening</term> <note>original: "cousening" — meaning cheating, swindling, or fraudulent.</note> witches, as is partly shown elsewhere in this discourse of mine, and as you may partly see by the contents of the following story. Not long since, a young woman (living at New Romney here in Kent), who was the daughter of one Mr. L. Stuppeny (formerly a <term>Jurat</term> <note>A magistrate or municipal officer in the "Cinque Ports" of England, such as New Romney.</note> of the same town, but deceased before this occurred), and later the wife of Thomas Eps (who is at this moment the Mayor of Romney), was afflicted with sickness. Overall, her mother and father-in-law, being deceived by a belief in a witch's supernatural power, went to a famous witch called Mother Baker, who lived not far from there at a place called Stone Street. 

<margin>A proven story concerning these matters.</margin>Following the deceptive customs of witches, she asked whether they suspected any bad neighbor. They answered that they did indeed doubt a woman near them (and yet that same woman was reputed to be a good person by the more honest and wiser sort of her neighbors). Nevertheless, the witch told them that there was great cause for their suspicion: "For that same woman," she said, "is the very person who brought about the young woman's destruction by making a heart of wax and pricking it with pins and needles." She also claimed that this neighbor had hidden the heart in some secret corner of the house. 

This being believed, the house was searched by reliable persons, but nothing could be found. When the witch (or "wise woman") was informed of this, she maintained her claim and insisted on going to the house where she herself (as she declared) would certainly find it. When she arrived, she used her "cunning"—which, as it happened, led to her own confusion, or at least to her being caught. For she did exactly what some of the wiser people suspected she would do: she secretly laid down such an image as she had previously described in a corner that had already been most diligently searched and looked into by others. By this means, her deception <note>original: "cousenage"</note> was notably exposed <note>original: "bewrayed"</note>. 

And I wish that all those who promote the belief in witches <note>original: "Witchmongers"</note> might pay for their wicked recourse to enchantments and their consultations with witches and those who claim to have familiar spirits, just as some of these people did by the order of the High Commissioners—which, partly out of respect for the neighborhood and partly for other considerations, I will leave unmentioned.

The means of how to find a thief is this: Turn your face to the East and <margin>Oh, most wonderful, hidden in the letters of Saint Helen’s holy name!</margin> make a cross upon a crystal with olive oil, and under the cross write these two words: Saint Helen. ## How to enclose a Spirit in a Crystal stone.

<margin>Requirements for cleanliness, fasting, and devotion.</margin>
The following operation is to have a Spirit enclosed into a crystal stone or beryl-glass <term>beryl-glass: a gemstone or crystal ball used for scrying or seeing spirits</term>, or into any other similar instrument, etc. First, during the new moon <note>original: "new of the ☽"</note>, being clothed in all new, fresh, and clean clothing and being shaven, fast that day on bread and water. All this being done, turn toward *Sitrael* and, kneeling, say this while holding the crystal stone in your hands:

<margin>Saint Bernard successfully outmatches the Devil despite all his cunning.</margin>
The first chapter of Saint John's Gospel, written in small letters, consecrated at a Mass, and hung about one's neck, is an incomparable amulet <note>original: "Periaptis"</note> or tablet, which delivers one from all witchcrafts and devilish practices. But it seems to me that if one were to hang a whole Testament, or rather a Bible, he might trick the Devil terribly. For indeed, this is what Saint Bernard would have done. The Devil told him that he could show him seven verses in the Book of Psalms <note>original: "Pſalter"</note> which, if repeated daily, would by themselves bring any man to Heaven and preserve him from Hell. But when Saint Bernard asked the Devil to tell him which verses they were, he refused, saying he might then be considered a fool for harming his own cause. "In that case," said Saint Bernard, "I will do well enough, for I will say the whole Book of Psalms every day." When the Devil heard him say this, he told him which the verses were, fearing that by reading the whole Book of Psalms daily, Bernard might earn too much merit for others. But if hanging Saint John's Gospel about the neck is so beneficial, what if one were to eat it?

->The making of Holy Water.<-

<margin>
Without an exorcism, salt does not become holy. <note>original: "Absque exorcismo sal non fit sanctus."</note> It is not appropriate to translate these four following Exorcisms into English; the name and power of God is so often abused in them for a vain and ridiculous purpose. <note>The author, Reginald Scot, was a skeptic who believed these rituals were superstitious nonsense and originally refused to translate the Latin to avoid spreading what he saw as "blasphemous" charms.</note>

I exorcise you, creature of salt, by the living God ✠ by the true God ✠ by the holy God ✠ by the God who commanded you to be cast into the water by Elisha <note>original: "Elizeum"</note> the Prophet, so that the barrenness of the water might be healed; that you may become exorcised salt for the salvation of believers; that you may be health of soul and body to all who take you, and let every phantom and wickedness, or the craftiness of Diabolical deceit, and every spirit, flee from wherever you are scattered, being adjured by him who is to come to judge the living and the dead, and the world by fire. Amen. Let us pray.

We humbly implore your boundless mercy, O Almighty eternal God, that you would deign to bless and sanctify with your piety this creature of salt, which you have given for the use of mankind, so that it may be health of mind and body to all who take it; so that whatever is touched or sprinkled by it may be free from all uncleanness and from every attack of spiritual wickedness, through our Lord Jesus Christ your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever. Amen.

->Another Witchcraft or Trickery practiced by the same Surgeon.<-

<margin>Three morsels: the first charmed with Christ's Birth, the second with his Passion, the third with his Resurrection.</margin>This surgeon treated a nobleman who lay sick with a fever <term>original: "Ague," a fever often associated with malaria, characterized by shivering and sweating.</term>. He offered him three pieces of a root to be eaten in three morsels. He said to the first, "I wish Christ had not been born"; to the second, "I wish he had not suffered"; and to the third, "I wish he had not risen again." Then, putting them around the sick man's neck, he said, "Be of good cheer; if he loses them, whoever takes them up shall likewise take away his fever." Otherwise, the charm was: "Jesus Christ who was born, deliver you from this infirmity; Jesus Christ who died, deliver you from this infirmity; Jesus Christ who rose again, deliver you from this infirmity." Then, five *Pater Nosters* <note>The "Our Father" prayer.</note> and five *Aves* <note>The "Hail Mary" prayer.</note> had to be said daily.

->Another Experiment for one bewitched.<-

<margin>A swindling physician and a foolish patient.</margin>Another such swindling physician persuaded a man who had abdominal swelling <term>original: "Timpany," a swelling of the abdomen caused by gas or fluid, often treated with suspicion of witchcraft.</term> that it was one old viper and two young ones being kept in his belly by witchcraft. But the physician was watched so that he could not sneak vipers into the patient's excrement after his purges. At length, he told the man that he would suffer the pains of childbirth if it were not prevented, and therefore he must put his hand into his own backside and pull out those worms from there. But the mother of the sick man, having been warned of this, said she could do that herself. Thus the swindler was stopped, the patient died only of abdominal swelling, and the knave fled out of the country.

<margin>Jean Bodin.</margin>
<margin>Misdirected zeal. <note>original Greek: "Kacozelia," meaning an inappropriate or faulty imitation.</note></margin>Monsieur Bodin <note>Jean Bodin, a French jurist and famous proponent of the witch hunts.</note> tells of a witch who, undertaking to cure a woman who was bewitched, caused a Mass to be sung at midnight in our Lady’s Chapel. When she had lain on top of the sick party and breathed certain words upon her, she was healed. In this, Bodin says she followed the example of Elisha the Prophet, who raised the Shunamite’s son <note>A reference to 2 Kings 4:34.</note>. This story must surely be true, for Goodman Hardivin of Blois <note>original: "Hardivin Blesensis"</note>, his host at the Sign of the Lion, told him the story.

## CHAP. XXVI.

### An Experiment of the Dead.

<margin>Promises and oaths mutually made between the Conjurer and the Spirit.</margin>
**F**irst, go and get a promise from some person who is to be executed <note>original: "put to death"</note>. Then lay your hand on your Book and swear this oath to him: *I, [Name], do swear and promise to you, [Name], to give alms on your behalf every month, and also to pray for you once every week, to say the Lord's Prayer for you, and to continue doing so all the days of my life, as God and the holy judgment help me, and by the contents of this Book, Amen.*

Then let him make his oath to you as follows, and let him say after you while laying his hand upon the Book: ✠ *I, [Name], do swear this oath to you, [Name], by God the Father Almighty, by God the Son Jesus Christ, and by his precious blood which has redeemed all the world—by which blood I trust to be saved at the general day of judgment—and by the powers thereof. I, [Name], do swear this oath to you, [Name], that my spirit which is now within my body shall not ascend, nor descend, nor go to any place of rest, but shall come to you, [Name]. It shall be very willing to remain with you, [Name], all the days of your life, and so to be bound to you, [Name], and to appear to you, [Name], in any crystal stone, glass, or other mirror, and so to take it for my resting-place. And as soon as my spirit has departed out of my body, it shall immediately be at your command; and on all days, nights, hours, and minutes, it shall be obedient to you, [Name], when called by you through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ. It shall immediately have common talk with you at all times, and come to open and declare to you, [Name], the truth of all things present, past, and to come, and how to work the Magic Art and all other noble sciences under the Throne of God. <margin>Note the penalty for breaking a promise with the Spirit.</margin> If I do not perform this oath and promise to you, [Name], but flee from any part of it, then I am to be condemned forever and ever. Amen.*

And finally, he says that all beautiful things whatsoever are soon subject to being bewitched; namely, handsome young men, fair women, those who are naturally born to be rich, handsome beasts, fine horses, thick crops <note>original: "rank corn"</note>, beautiful trees, etc. Yes, a friend of his told him that he saw someone break a precious stone into pieces with his eye. And he tells all this as soberly as though it were true. And if it were true, honest women could be witches despite all the Inquisitors; nor could any woman avoid being a witch unless she locked herself up in a room.

### CHAP. XXI.

*What miracles believers in witchcraft <note>original: "Witchmongers"</note> report to have been done by witches' words, etc. Contradictions of believers in witchcraft among themselves; how beasts are cured by these means; of bewitched butter; a charm against witches, and a counter-charm; the effect of charms and words proved by L. Varius to be wonderful.*

If I should try to list all charms, I would be undertaking an infinite work. For the writers on witchcraft hold the opinion that almost anything may be accomplished by them; and that it does not matter whether the words of the charm are understandable or not, so long as the charmer has a steady intention to bring his desire about. And then, what is it that cannot be done by words?
<margin>L. Varius, Book on Fascination <note>original: "lib. de fascin"</note>, book 1, chapter 5.</margin>
For *L. Varius* says that old women have weakened and killed children with words, and have made pregnant women miscarry; they have made men pine away to death; they have killed horses, deprived sheep of their milk; *transformed men into beasts, flown in the air, tamed and stopped wild beasts, driven all harmful cattle and vermin from crops, vines, and herbs, stopped serpents, etc. and all with words.* He even says that with certain words spoken 
<margin>According to Ovid's saying of Proteus and Medea, which he indeed alleged for that purpose: "Now as water, now as a bird, now as an ox, now as a deer, he departed" <note>original: "Nunc aqua, nunc ales, modo bos, modo cervus abibat"</note>.</margin>
into a bull's ear by a witch, the bull has fallen to the ground as if dead. Yes, some by virtue of words have walked upon a sharp sword and walked upon hot glowing coals without harm; with words (he says) very heavy weights and burdens have been lifted; and with words wild horses, wild bulls, and also mad dogs have been tamed; with words they have killed worms and other vermin, and stopped all manner of bleeding and discharges <note>original: "fluxes"</note>; with words all the diseases in a man's body are healed and wounds cured; arrows are pulled out of men's bones with wonderful strangeness and skill. Yes (he says), there are many who can heal all bites of dogs, or stings of serpents, or any other poison: and all with nothing but spoken words. And that which...

# Book 12: The Discovery of Charms, etc.

...the same was so troubled with such a horrible noise and such earthquakes that, if the door had not been opened, we would have thought the house was going to fall on our heads. *Thomas Aquinas* <note>A hugely influential 13th-century philosopher and theologian.</note>, a primary writer on this subject, allows for conjurations against changelings <note>Children believed to be fairy or demonic substitutes for human infants.</note> and in various other cases, about which I will say more regarding the word *Fidoni*.

->### A special Charm to preserve all Cattle from Witchcraft.###<-

<margin>In any case, observe the festival time, or else you ruin everything.</margin>
At Easter, you must take certain drops of wax that lie at the top of the holy Paschal candle and make a little wax candle from them. On some Sunday morning early <note>original: "rathe"</note>, light it and hold it so that the wax may drop upon and between the ears of the beast, while saying, "In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and double-f" <note>original: "In Nomine Patris, & Filii, & duplex ff."</note>. Then, rub a little of that same wax between the horns and on the ears. After rubbing it, stick the remaining wax in the shape of a cross around the stable or stall, or over the door where the cattle go in and out; by doing this, all your cattle shall never be bewitched. 

Otherwise, *Jacobus de Chusa*, a Carthusian monk <note>A 15th-century theologian known for his writings on the supernatural.</note>, shows how bread, water, and salt are conjured. He says that if a person or beast receives holy bread and holy water for nine days together, along with three Our Fathers <note>original: "Paters"</note> and three Hail Marys <note>original: "Aves"</note> in honor of the Trinity and of Saint Hubert <note>The patron saint of hunters, often invoked against rabies.</note>, it preserves that man or beast from all diseases and defends them against all assaults of witchcraft, of Satan, or of a mad dog, and so on.

<margin>Léonard Vair, *Book on Fascination*, Chapter 1 <note>original: "L. Vair. lib. de fascin. c. 1."</note></margin>
Look, this is the kind of material maintained to be at least effective, if not wholesome, by all Papists <note>A derogatory term for Catholics used by the author.</note> and "witchmongers" <note>The author's term for people who promote the belief in and persecution of witches.</note>, and especially by the most recent and arrogant writers. But to prove these things are effective—God knows their reasons are base and absurd. 

For they write in such a way that they take the matter in question as a proven fact. For instance, Léonard Vair writes in his book that there is no doubt about this supernatural matter because a number of writers agree on it, a number of stories confirm it, many poets handle the same argument, and there is a law against it in the Twelve Tables <note>The earliest code of Roman law.</note>. He also argues it is true because the consensus of the common people is fully behind it; because immoderate praise is considered a kind of witchcraft; and because old women have used such superstitious means to preserve themselves from it. He further argues it is true because those who take away the credibility of such miracles are mocked, and because Solomon says, "The fascination of wickedness obscures good things" <note>original: "Fascinatio malignitatis obscurat bona" (Wisdom of Solomon 4:12)</note>, and because the Apostle Paul says, "O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you?" <note>original: "O insensati Galatae, quis vos fascinavit?" (Galatians 3:1)</note>, and because it is written, "They that fear you shall see me" <note>original: "Qui timent te, videbunt me" (Psalm 119:74)</note>. 

Finally, he says that—lest you should seem to distrust or detract anything from the credit of so many grave men, from histories, and from the common opinion of all men—he intends in no way to prove that there is miraculous working by witchcraft and fascination <note>term: fascination - in this context, the power to harm or influence people through a look or spell; "the evil eye."</note>. And so, he proceeds according to his promise.

->### CHAPTER 22.###<-

->**Lawful Charms, or rather medicinal cures for diseased cattle. The Charm of Charms, and the power thereof.**<-

<margin>Direct and lawful means of curing cattle, etc.</margin>
But if you desire to learn true and lawful "charms" to cure diseased cattle—even those that seem to have extraordinary sickness, or appear to be bewitched or (as they say) "strangely taken"—look in Barnabe Googe’s <note>A 16th-century poet and translator of works on agriculture.</note> third book treating of cattle, and perhaps you shall find some good medicine or cure for them. Or, if you wish to see more ancient material, read the four books on the subject by Vegetius <note>A late Roman author whose work on veterinary medicine remained influential for centuries.</note>. Or, if you are unlearned, seek a skilled cattle-doctor <note>original: "bullock-leech"</note>. 

If all this will not serve, then set the patience of Job before your eyes. Never think that a poor old woman can supernaturally alter the notable course which God has appointed among his creatures. If it had been God's pleasure to permit such a course, he would no doubt have given notice in his Word that he had given...

# The Discovery of Witchcraft: Chapter 29

## A Permission to Depart

Depart from the sight of this crystal stone in peace for a time, but be ready to appear in it again at any time or times I shall call you, by virtue of our Lord *Jesus Christ* and by the power of the words written in this book, appearing visibly as these words are rehearsed. I constrain you, Spirit [Name], by the divinity of God to be obedient to these words spoken, upon pain of everlasting condemnation, both in this world and in the world to come. Let it be done, let it be done, let it be done. **Amen.**

## CHAPTER 29

### *When to talk with spirits, and how to get true answers to find a thief.*

<margin>This is condemned as utter foolishness by the Doctors of the Church, such as *Chrysostom* in his commentary on *Matthew* <note>original: "Chrysost. sup. Matth."</note>, *Gregory* in his sermon on the *Epiphany of the Lord* <note>original: "Gregor. in homil. sup. Epiphan. Domini"</note>, and others.</margin>

The days and hours of Saturn, Mars, and the Moon are best for performing all the arts of necromancy, for speaking with spirits, and for discovering a theft to get a true answer about it or any other similar matter. In the days and hours of the Sun, Jupiter, and Venus, it is best to perform all experiments of love, to obtain favor <note>original: "purchase grace"</note>, to become invisible, and to perform any operation whatsoever, provided the Moon is in a suitable sign. 

* When you are working to find a thief, see that the Moon is in an earthy sign, such as Taurus ♉, Virgo ♍, or Capricorn ♑, or an air sign, such as Gemini ♊, Libra ♎, or Aquarius ♒. 
* And if it is for love, favor, or grace, let the Moon be in a fire sign, such as Aries ♈, Leo ♌, or Sagittarius ♐. 
* For hatred, let the Moon be in a water sign, such as Cancer ♋, Scorpio ♏, or Pisces ♓. 
* For any other experiment, let the Moon be in Aries ♈. 
* And if you find the Sun and the Moon in the same sign, which is called an even number, then you may write, consecrate, conjure, and prepare all manner of things that you wish to do, etc.

### *To speak with Spirits.*

Call these names: **Azimoth**, **Beltmoth**, **Lymock**, and say this: *I conjure you up by the names of the angels* **Satur** *and* **Azimor**, *that you attend to me in this hour, and send to me a spirit called* **Sagrigrit**, *so that he may fulfill my command and desire, and so that he can also understand my words for one or two years, or as long as I wish.*
