# 64 Book II. A Discourse concerning Infernal Spirits.

<margin>The Nature of Hell.</margin>
43. For the nature of their home is such that their torment is greatly worsened by it, because the extremes of the four elements are transformed there into a single principle of wrath and irritation. The excesses of cold and heat, drought and moisture, are continually raging among them through alternating cycles <note>original: "intercourse"</note>. Nor is there any light or brightness to be seen within their courts, except for that which comes from their fiery eyes, appearing as a deadly glance or glimmer—sudden fiery flashes and sparking, like the ignition of gunpowder, or "fulminating gold" <note>original: "Aurum fulminans," a volatile and explosive gold-based chemical compound used here as a comparison</note> as a likeness.

<margin>The food of Devils.</margin>
44. And just as every kind of being feeds upon something of its own nature, property, and element—whether it be plant, animal, or mineral—so the Devils are not without food, drink, or clothing, according to the quality of their own Kingdom. They have fruits springing and growing before them of hellish, sour, and poisonous natures; these are real and physical <note>original: "palpable"</note> to them, and not imaginary or symbolic, even though to us they are magical and invisible. This is not to be wondered at if we consider the nature of the human soul, which exists in a middle state <note>original: "In Media Natura," referring to the soul's position between the physical and spiritual realms</note>. For if the soul does not feed upon the internal and substantial Word (which is the very Bread of Life itself), it must by necessity chew on <note>original: "ruminate"</note> something else: namely, the fruits of sin, which it takes in and drinks up as an ox drinks water. Thus, sin becomes tangible, glutting, and filling to the soul; indeed, it becomes as substantial to the soul as dirt or ink on fine white linen is to our physical eyes. Nor can the soul be freed from these spots until the "water above the firmament" <note>a biblical reference to celestial or divine grace</note> washes them away.

<margin>Their food in the Astral source.</margin>
45. Also, regarding their astral source, they are not without food when they enter into it; for the "gas" of the air and "blas" of the water <term>gas and blas: 17th-century chemical terms coined by Jan Baptist van Helmont; 'gas' refers to a refined spiritual essence of air, while 'blas' refers to the motive or astral force of the stars and water</term> provide their nourishment while they stay here, as was stated before. They take these influences of the air and water into their own boundary <note>original: "Limbus"</note> and convert them into their own poisonous natures. This is similar to how filthy toads and other venomous beasts create poison from sweet and wholesome herbs, converting them into a nature like their own. On the contrary, poisonous herbs are converted into good and wholesome nourishment by other clean animals.

<margin>Their Speech.</margin>
46. And as the infernal troops are considered in relation to the four elements, they have a distinct and peculiar tone or language, which they use and speak among one another, just as mortals do. However, they have utterly lost the nobility <note>original: "dignity"</note> of their sounds according to their original eternal nature. They are likewise totally corrupted in their pronunciation or dialect since they fell from their first heavenly glory; so their speech is harsh, mournful, and terrible, like the fruits they feed upon and the life they live in. This corruption is very apparent in the kingdom of this world in the divided languages of every region, which correspond to the constellation under which they are situated. The true and magical Language of Nature is hidden from all the countries of the earth.

<margin>What Language they affect.</margin>
47. But when they appear in the outward elements <note>meaning the physical world</note>, they many times express themselves in *Irish*, *Welsh*, *Latin*, or *Russian*, which are the languages they most prefer <note>original: "affect"</note> when responding to conjurations or magical contracts. Therefore, if any magician who is ignorant of these languages should at any time summon <note>original: "Raise"</note> or drive out <note>original: "Exorcise"</note> such spirits, he must be careful to confine them to his mother tongue, lest their gibberish prove completely unintelligible. For as everything appears in the form it most likes or is addicted to, even so the spirits have their distinct preferences, passions, and postures—in word, clothing, shape, and gesture. Thus, the magician must be cautious when performing exorcisms with them, ensuring he restricts them to a specific place, posture, shape, and language to suit his intentions without hindrance.

<margin>Their unconstancy.</margin>
48. For they are very variable and inconsistent in their dealings with mankind, and they will not stand by anything unless they have been bound by the obligations of words, symbols <note>original: "Characters"</note>, and curses <note>original: "Imprecations"</note>—unless the skill of the exorcist is so great that he is able to confine them into a Magical Triad <note>a grouping of three magical names or principles used for binding</note>, which has the certain power of obliging or compelling them to speak the truth and nothing false in all

# Chapter 5: Of Infernal Spirits, Devils, and Spirits. 65

...all their answers or information. However, with those miserable men and women who have made covenants and contracts <note>original: "Indentures," a legal agreement binding one person to work for another</note> for their body, soul, and labor—with those people, I say, the spirits keep no faith. Nor are the spirits subject to their commands; on the contrary, they keep these people trapped and subjected to their will and power until they have ended their lives in destruction.

<margin>Their Power.</margin>
49. Yet even the most powerful princes of the hellish realm do not have the slightest ability to destroy even the lowliest human being without the consent of the soul’s mind and senses. Until the soul’s will is opened to the spirit, its threats, tricks, and strategies are without any power or force, as useless as the nerves of a dead man. Every evil spirit naturally boasts as if the whole world were at its command and every soul were subject to its authority and whim, along with all the goods and possessions of the physical world.

<margin>When they are called up.</margin>
50. When an evil spirit is raised by conjurations <note>rituals or spells used to summon spirits</note> without a formal league or pact, these summoned spirits are exceedingly fraudulent and deceitful. They act like stubborn servants who perform their master’s will only by force, and not out of any natural obedience to his commands. But with those people they have made a pact with, they are constant and eager to help, employing them as agents for the destruction of other people and their property. By being "married" to such people, they even become one with them, being incorporated into them so that they are no different from devils in human form <note>original: "incarnate Devils"</note>—except that the spark of divine light (which was God's gift to lead one to repentance) is not totally extinguished until the body dies.

<margin>Offerings made to them.</margin>
51. From those who enter into covenants with these unstable spirits, the spirits daily obtain fumigations <note>the use of smoke or incense in a ritual</note>, fragrances, and offerings—or sacrifices of blood, fire, wine, ointments, incense, fruits, waste, herbs, resins, minerals, and other ingredients. Through a magical cause, these offerings give the spirits more influence and authority over the bewitched person, allowing them to creep into the person's affections, piercing even through their bones and marrow. This continues until they have so accustomed the person to their service that it becomes their daily bread and only delight to commit every villainy and abomination that the malicious and subtle urging of Satan leads them to.

<margin>The Conclusion.</margin>
52. Thus, I have attempted <note>original: "Essayed"</note> to illustrate the natures of infernal beings. Nevertheless, this is a subject so intricate and vast that explaining it is very difficult because of the variety of their natures within the source of darkness where they live, move, eat, breathe, and dwell. They have innumerable qualities, actions, and passions that are utterly unknown and incomprehensible to us humans. To attempt a full demonstration of this subject would require deeper contemplation than the matter deserves, considering there are so many shapeshifters <note>original: "Protei," referring to Proteus, the Greek sea-god who could change into any form</note> and changelings in that gloomy kingdom who never remain in the same nature, property, or form for even an hour. They may be compared to the swiftness of the winds or the likeness of fast-running waters that pass away like a thought and are no longer remembered. So it is with the spirits of darkness, whose life is pure anguish and instability, moving from one sorrow to another for all eternity.

# Chapter VI.

### *Treating the Nature, Power, and Forms of Charms, Periaphs <note>original: "Periaphs," charms or amulets worn on the body to ward off evil or disease</note>, Amulets, Pentacles, Conjurations, Ceremonies, etc.*

<margin>Signs shown before spirits appear.</margin>
1. Before appearances are made, and after the forms of conjuration <note>the act of calling upon or summoning a spirit</note> are repeated, the infernal spirits produce various wonderful displays, noises, and attempts as forerunners to their arrival. In the first attempts of beginners in conjuration, they are accompanied by noises, tremblings, flashes, howlings, and most dreadful shrieks. As they make further progress and gain experience, the spirits approach closer to this physical world <note>original: "Elemental nature"</note> until, by degrees, they can become clearly visible to their exorcist.

<margin>An account of a magician.</margin>
2. When *Chiancungi* and his sister *Napala* first attempted to call up spirits, they began with the spirit **Bokim**, in the twentieth degree. They lined an underground vault with black cloth on both the ceiling and the floor. Having drawn the Circle of the Order of Thrones, with the seven planets and their magical symbols <note>original: "Characters"</note> in the center, they proceeded to the ceremonies of conjuration. After they had frequently repeated the forms of calling and nothing had yet appeared, they grew so desperate that they abandoned the circle and every defensive symbol or ceremony. Finally, they turned to the most accursed and detestable branch of magic, which consists of pacts or confederacies <note>formal agreements or alliances with demons</note>. Having summoned the aforementioned spirit **Bokim** by a solemn league, they obtained 155 years of life from the spirit, entering into a covenant for their bodies, souls, and works.

<margin>His actions.</margin>
3. In this condemned life, they continued to perform strange wonders in every country. With the help of this magician, the *Tartars* <note>a historical term for various Central Asian and Northern Asian peoples</note> destroyed more than 100 ships belonging to *China*. He brought many losses upon that kingdom regarding their children, fruits, corn, silk, and navigation. He could frequently fly <note>original: "transport himself"</note> through the air and carry a thousand-pound weight in one hand, to the astonishment of all who knew him. He had many public contests with magicians from other countries—trials of skill in the magical arts—wherein he was said to excel everyone who had lived before him.

<margin>Another magician.</margin>
4. Another such person was *Louis Gaufridi*, a *French* priest who had made a pact with the Devil and served him for 14 years in these detestable works. He sacrificed infants to him, worshipped him in a revolting form, and tempted others to join their magical society or nocturnal meetings <note>original: "Conventions"</note>. In these meetings, it is reported that they always feasted on a variety of delicacies which, though they seemed delicious, were nevertheless tasteless and unsavory.

<margin>What charms are.</margin>
5. Moving on from these accounts, something shall be said of *charms* and *spells*, which are categorized in the following way: First, amulets that are engraved and molded in the fashion of money or coins; these serve to provoke love and intimacy in a desired person when hung around the neck during certain planetary hours. Second, spells or charms written on parchment with magical symbols, used as periaphs to cure diseases or to make one brave, mindful, and steadfast. Third, corselets <note>here, a type of ritual necklace</note>, which are an ancient *Danish* charm consisting of necklaces made of thunderstones <note>prehistoric stone tools or fossils once believed to have fallen from the sky during storms</note> engraved with magical letters to resist all harmful influences and the danger of lightning.

<margin>Pentacles.</margin>
6. Pentacles are a fourth type of accessory used by conjurers, charmers, and magicians. They are made with five corners, representing the five senses, and their specific operation is inscribed upon those corners. They are composed of fine double-layered linen with wax-cloth <note>original: "Cere-cloth," cloth treated with wax or oil</note> in between. The magician holds this figure in his hand, lifting it from the hem of his garment to which it is attached, when the spirits that are raised are stubborn and rebellious, refusing to comply with the ceremonies and rites of magic.

<margin>Their power.</margin>
7. Also, by holding forth *pentacles* and speaking these words: **Glauron, Amoza,**

Amozula, Beoz, Beozka, Bezoald, and Anepheraton—if these names are repeated in that moment, the evil spirits possessing the bodies of bewitched people are cruelly tortured and dazed. By the frequent repetition of these names, they are forced at last to depart, assisted by the Exorcism of the sixth Canon for the order of Seraphims <note>the highest rank of angels in the celestial hierarchy</note>.

<margin>Telesms.</margin>
8. When magicians perform conjurations by moonlight in the mountains or valleys, they use another sort of charm known as <term>Telesms</term> <note>original: "Telefms"; talismans or magical objects inscribed with symbols</note>. They bury these within a hundred paces of the place where the magic circle is drawn—positioned toward the East, West, North, and South. Such spells have the secret power to prevent any living creature from coming near them until their ritual is finished, except for the infernal spirit whose presence they so ardently desire.

<margin>For diseases.</margin>
9. Some spells are made using edible substances with magical symbols <note>original: "Characters"</note> marked upon them; these are given to treat <term>agues</term> <note>fevers and chills</note>, headaches, epilepsy, <term>the Mother</term> <note>original: "Mother"; a historical term for hysteria or respiratory distress believed to be caused by the womb</note>, and similar ailments. These are especially powerful in their operation when the person is unaware that they have taken a charm; I know of many such instances that have had wonderful effects. However, as for philtres, potions, and love-charms <note>original: "Love-cups"</note>, these proceed from natural causes instead—whether their effects are to afflict someone with disease, to poison them, or to provoke love for a person they actually despise. These are not to be counted among true charms because their effect is purely physical, arising from a natural cause.

<margin>Fumigations.</margin>
10. To speak further on the nature of conjuration, magicians spend much of their time performing <term>fumigations</term> <note>the burning of incense or other materials to create smoke</note> to the spirits they intend to summon. Their incense is categorized according to the nature of the spirit under any of the seven planets. Ancient conjurers were very precise in observing these rules, though in these days it is often forgotten as something unnecessary, or even too dangerous to include among the ceremonies of conjuration. We will set down here a division of fumigations according to the influence of the planets and the orders of spirits in the following manner.

<margin>For Saturn.</margin>
11. Fumigations for **Saturn** are made of frankincense trees, pepper-wort roots, <term>storax</term> <note>a fragrant resin</note>, and galbanum. By these, the spirits Varbas, Cozban, Stilkon, Idos, and others—all those of the first order of <term>astringency</term> <note>in old medicine, Saturn was associated with cold and "binding" qualities</note>—are appeased and summoned when the incense is placed upon a <term>tripod</term> <note>a three-legged stand for a brazier</note> during the hour of Saturn, according to planetary time. These fumigations make these spirits appear like old men with long, flowing beards and haggard faces; or like serpents, cats, wolves, badgers, and panthers; or like old men in armor; or like ranks of trumpeters.

<margin>Jupiter.</margin>
12. For spirits under **Jupiter**, they use <term>Lignum Aloes</term> <note>original: "Lignum Aloes"; aloeswood or agarwood</note>, ash tree seeds <note>original: "Ashen-Keys"</note>, <term>benzoin</term> <note>original: "Benjamin"; a fragrant balsamic resin</note>, storax, peacock feathers, and <term>lapis lazuli</term>, mixing them with the blood of a stork, a swallow, or a deer, with brains also added. The incense is lit during Jupiter's hour and in a place appropriate to his nature. By this sacrifice, the spirits of the next order are called up, appearing like glorious kings with many attendants and great pomp, preceded by heralds, banner-bearers, guards, and all sorts of musical instruments.

<margin>Mars.</margin>
13. They perform fumigations for those spirits of the Order of Powers who are under **Mars** in the planetary division. These are made with aromatic gum, bdellium, euphorbium, loadstone, white and black hellebore, with sulfur added to make them into an amalgam <note>a mixture</note> using human blood and the blood of a black cat. These mixtures are said to be exceedingly magical. They claim that even without any other addition, this fumigation is able by itself to make such spirits appear before the exorcist. When they appear, they come brandishing weapons and wearing shining armor, looking terrible. Yet they are inferior in power to the spirits of Saturn, though they can likewise show themselves as lions, wolves, tigers, bears, and all other cruel or ravenous beasts.

<margin>Sol.</margin>
14. They do the same for the spirits under **Sol** (the Sun), who belong to the Order of Thrones. They burn saffron, musk, laurel, cinnamon, <term>ambergris</term> <note>a rare substance from sperm whales</note>, cloves, myrrh, frankincense, and the balsam tree, mixed together with the brain of an eagle and the blood of a white cock. These are made into pills or little balls and put upon the tripod. Their appearances take the form of castles, gardens,

<margin>Venus.</margin>
15. Under *Venus* are the spirits of the sixth order in the Powers; their appearances are very stately, matching the nature of the planet. They appear as courtiers, ladies, princes, queens, infants, children, and bring fragrant smells. The <term>fumigations</term> <note>incense or smoke produced by burning specific substances</note> appropriate for them are roses, coral, <term>agarwood</term> <note>original: "Lignum Aloes"</note>, and <term>spermaceti</term> <note>original: "Sperma Ceti"; a waxy substance found in the head of sperm whales</note>, mixed with the brains of sparrows and the blood of pigeons, to be burned while a song is performed.

<margin>Mercury.</margin>
16. *Mercury* sends horsemen, fishermen, laborers, priests, students, servants, and so on. Also: foxes, serpents, dogs, hares, hyenas, hydras, and other monstrous animals. For him, they burn frankincense, mastic, <term>cinquefoil</term> <note>original: "Cinkfoyl"; a plant in the rose family</note> mixed with the brain of a fox and the blood of a magpie.

<margin>Luna.</margin>
17. Spirits under *Luna* <note>the Moon</note> are like ghosts and shadows, very ghastly to behold; though they take human shape, they are sometimes male and sometimes female. Fumigations offered to them consist of dried frogs, white poppy seed, bull eyes, camphor, and frankincense, mixed with goose blood and the menstrual blood of women.

<margin>Why such ceremonies are effective.</margin>
18. These are the categories of fumigations. It cannot be denied that in many ceremonies of this kind, there is a great inherent power according to the doctrines of <term>Sympathy and Antipathy</term> <note>the Renaissance belief that objects are naturally drawn to or repelled by things that share their spiritual qualities</note>. By this principle, everything is drawn to its likeness in the "Ideal" world, whether by words or actions, according to the saying: "In words, herbs, and stones, power lies hidden" <note>original: "In verbis, herbis & lapidibus latet virtus"</note>. Thus, the ceremonies and charms—along with other circumstances used by magicians—are undoubtedly effective in accomplishing the work they undertake: namely, *the calling up and exorcising of infernal spirits by conjurations.*

### CHAPTER VII.

->*Being the Conclusion of the Whole; wherein various ancient Spells, Charms, Incantations, and Exorcisms are briefly discussed.*<-

<margin>Charms.</margin>
1. **B**esides what the author has recorded, there are many other *spells* and *charms* which tradition has left to posterity. Many of these are effective for their intended purpose, as described in the previous chapter regarding the orders of fumigations. Furthermore, there are *magical characters* <note>symbols or sigils</note> attributed to the planets, from which <term>telesms</term> <note>talismans</note>, <term>periapts</term> <note>charms worn on the body</note>, amulets, and <term>philtres</term> <note>love potions</note> are composed. These are created through burials, writings, bindings, engravings, and <term>alligations</term> <note>the act of tying a charm to a person or object</note> to achieve various goals during specific astrological hours. These include conquering enemies, curing diseases, overturning cities, stopping floods, making bodies invulnerable, and the like; all of which are achieved through these methods with the assistance of the imagination.

<margin>Natural Operations.</margin>
2. Yet there are many natural compositions which have stupendous effects on their own, without the help of superstition. The mixing of things has a two-fold power: First, when celestial virtues are properly arranged in any natural body, so that one object contains various influences of superior powers. The second is from the artificial mixture and composition of natural things among themselves, in a certain proportion intended to harmonize with the heavens under specific constellations. This proceeds from the natural correspondence between things, by which amazing results are achieved, as <term>Agrippa</term> <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535), a famous German polymath and occult writer</note> declares in *Book 1, Chapter 35*.

<margin>Places ascribed to the seven Planets.</margin>
3. Just as certain fumigations are assigned to every planet, certain *places* are designated for the ceremonies of conjuration for the spirits under them. Magicians choose these locations when they begin their works of darkness. To *Saturn* are assigned dark, melancholy places: vaults, tombs, monasteries, empty houses, dens, caves, and pits. To *Jupiter*: theaters, schools, music houses, and courtrooms <note>original: "Judgment seats"</note>. To *Mars*: fields where battles have been fought, bake-houses, glass-works, <term>slaughterhouses</term> <note>original: "Shambles"</note>, and places of execution. To *Sol* <note>the Sun</note>: palaces, mountains,

<margin>Spells.</margin>
4. In the same way, *spells* and *charms* are adapted to the effect they are intended to produce, according to their material, form, and the place where they are composed. For example, to procure *love*, they bury rings, ribbons, seals, pictures, looking-glasses, etc., in <term>stews</term> <note>original: "stews"; brothels or bathhouses</note>, baths, or beds, so that in such places these items may acquire some <term>venereal faculty</term> <note>powers associated with Venus, the goddess of love</note>. When they gather herbs or other ingredients, they choose the hour and place when the planets that rule those herbs have dominion. They always remember to turn their faces to the East or South when <term>Saturnine</term>, <term>Martial</term>, or <term>Jovial</term> <note>herbs associated with Saturn, Mars, or Jupiter</note> herbs are gathered, because their principal <term>houses</term> <note>astrological signs</note> are Southern signs. For *Venereal*, *Mercurial*, or *Lunary* herbs, they must look toward the *West* or *North*, because their houses are chiefly Northern signs. Yet, in any *Solar* or *Lunar* operations, the actual position of the Sun and Moon must be respected during the work.

<margin>Secret Conclusions.</margin>
5. Colors are also highly regarded among magicians, according to the planet. For *Saturn*, they use black, leaden, and brown. For *Jupiter*: sapphire, <term>vernal</term> <note>spring-like</note>, green, purple, and golden. For *Mars*: red, burning, violet, bloody, and iron colors. For the *Sun*: golden, saffron, scarlet, etc. For *Venus*, *Mercury*, and *Luna*: white, fair, green, ruddy, and pleasant mixed colors. In the same way, they ascribe colors to the twelve houses of the zodiac. According to the planets, they also have certain compositions for fire that produce wonderful effects; for instance, lamps made of serpent skins will make serpents appear. Oil that has stood under grapes, when lighted, makes the chamber appear full of grapes. <term>Centaury</term> <note>a flowering plant used in folk medicine</note> mixed with the blood of a <term>lapwing</term> <note>a species of bird</note> makes people look like giants, and in the open air, it will make the stars seem to move up and down in the <term>elements</term> <note>the sky or atmosphere</note>. The fat of a hare lighted in a lamp will cause women to be exceedingly merry and witty. Candles composed of things that are *Saturnine* raise terror and melancholy in the person who lights them, and in those who are illuminated by them.

<margin>The Candle of Life.</margin>
6. Natural things have such wonderful effects when they are matched to their proper hours and constellations, and also when they are used to prove effects that the nature of the thing produces by itself, though to a weaker degree. To raise *tempests*, magicians burn the liver of a chameleon on a house top. To cause strange sights, they hang the gall of an ox over their beds. To bring *apparitions* and *spirits*, they make a strange <term>fume</term> <note>smoke or incense</note> from a man's gall and the eyes of a black cat; <term>Agrippa</term> <note>original: "Agrippa"; Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535), a famous German polymath and occult writer</note> says he has often experimented with this. There is also a strange magical candle described among *chemical authors* which, when lighted, foretells the death of the person to whom it belongs. The method is this: they take a large amount of venous blood, lukewarm as it comes out of the vein, which is <term>chemically</term> <note>original: "Chymically"</note> prepared with spirit of wine and other ingredients, and finally made into a candle. Once kindled, it never goes out until the death of the person whose blood it is made of; for when he is sick or in danger, it burns dim and troubled, and when he is dead, it is quite extinguished. A learned man wrote an entire treatise on this composition, titled *De Biolychnio*, or, *The Lamp of Life* <note>original: "De Biolychnio"; Latin for "Concerning the Lamp of Life"</note>.

<margin>That Characters are compacts.</margin>
7. But to proceed to the nature of *characters*, <term>sigils</term> <note>inscribed symbols used in magic</note>, and other ceremonies, we find that these are used not only by those who pretend to command all sorts of spirits, but also by those who make <term>compacts</term> <note>binding contracts or agreements with spirits</note> and have sold themselves to the Devil. This instance is sufficient to prove what a wise man has asserted: although evil spirits have so blinded men's eyes as to make them believe they are defended by such ceremonies, and that these characters are defenses against the Devil’s malice, yet these very *characters*, *sigils*, <term>lamins</term> <note>thin plates of metal inscribed with magical symbols</note>, etc., are *compacts* themselves. The Devils originally disguised them with strange repetitions in weird languages.

8. So we have grounds to believe that no one is able to call up any spirit absolutely without a *compact*. But whoever has pretended to be famous in

<meta>This page continues the author's argument that the biblical story of Job does not support the existence of powerful witches, as Job attributed his suffering to God rather than to supernatural agents or magic.</meta>

<page-num>60</page-num>
<header>BOOK V. The Discovery</header>

### The history of Job.

...God to lay His hand upon him. Insofar as *Job* attributed no part of his calamity to devils, witches, nor even to conjurers or their enchantments, as we have learned to do today. Neither did he sin, nor did God do any wrong, when Job laid the charge to Him; but we dishonor God greatly when we attribute either the power or the nature of God the Creator to a creature.

<margin>John Calvin on Job 2, Sermon 8. Musculus, Common Places.</margin>
*Calvin* says that we detract much from God’s glory and omnipotence when we say He only gives Satan "leave" to do it; which is, he says, to mock God’s justice. It is such a foolish assertion that if donkeys could speak, they would speak more wisely than that. For a temporal judge does not say to the hangman, "I give you leave to hang this offender," but commands him to do it. But the supporters of the witches' omnipotence say, "Do you not see how really and palpably the Devil tempted and plagued *Job*?" I answer first: that there is no physical Devil named or seen in any part of that story. Second: that it was the hand of God that did it. Third: that as there is no connection between the person of a witch and the person of a devil, so there was not any conference or practice between them in this case.

<margin>John Calvin in his sermon upon Job.</margin>
And regarding the communication between God and the Devil, look at what *Calvin* says, writing (or rather preaching on purpose) upon that passage where they think they have such a great advantage: "When Satan is said to appear before God, it is not done in a specific physical place, but the Scripture speaks that way to accommodate our limited understanding." <note>original: "rudeness"</note> Certainly, the Devil in this and such cases is an instrument to work God’s will, and not his own; and therefore it is an ignorant and ungodly saying (as *Calvin* judges it) to affirm that God only "permits" and "suffers" the Devil. For if Satan were left at his own liberty, he says, we would be overwhelmed in an instant. And undoubtedly, if he had power to hurt the body, there would be no way to resist; for he would come invisibly upon us and strike us on the head; indeed, he would watch for the best people and dispatch them while they were about some wicked act. If they say God commands him, no one argues with them; but that God should "give him leave," I say with *Calvin* that the Devil is not in such favor with God as to obtain any such request at His hands.

<margin>John Calvin on Job 1, Sermon 5.</margin>
And whereas by our witch-believers' <note>original: "Witchmongers"</note> opinions and arguments, the witch recruits the Devil, and the Devil asks leave of God to plague whomever the witch is disposed to hurt, there is not (as I have said) any such physical communication between the Devil and a witch as witch-believers imagine. Neither is God moved at all by Satan's petition, who has no such favor or grace with Him as to obtain anything at His hands.

<margin>The Hammer of Witches, part 1, question 1. The same, part 1, question 4.</margin>
But *Malleus Maleficarum* <note>The "M. Mal." refers to the "Malleus Maleficarum," a famous 15th-century manual for hunting witches.</note> and its friends deny that there were any witches in *Job's* time; indeed, the witch-believers are content to say that there were none found to practice this art in *Christ's* time, from His birth to His death, even for the span of thirty-three years. "If there had been any," they say, "they would have been spoken of there." Regarding the authority of the Book of *Job*, there is no question that it is very canonical and authentic. However, many writers, both among the Jews and others, are of the opinion that *Moses* was the author of this book, and that he set it as a mirror before the people so that the children of *Abraham* (from whose race he himself came) might know that God showed favor to others who were not of the same lineage, and so they might be ashamed of their wickedness, seeing how a non-Jew <note>original: "uncircumcised Painime"</note> had conducted himself so well. Upon this argument *Calvin* (though he had written on the same) says that because it is uncertain whether it was a historical event <note>original: "Res gesta"</note> or a parable <note>original: "Exempli gratia"</note>, we must leave it in suspense. "Nevertheless," he says, "let us take that which is beyond all doubt: namely, that the Holy Ghost dictated the book so that the Jews should know that God has always had a people to serve Him throughout the world, even among those who were not Jews, nor separated from other nations."

<margin>Note what is said regarding the Book of Job.</margin>
However, I for my part do not deny the truth of the story; though indeed I must confess that I think there was no such physical interlude between God...

### *Of Charms, etc.* Devils and Spirits. CHAPTER 7.

...hour of the creation <note>original: "Composition"</note>, and the posture or appearance of the image.

<margin>Of images and what is achieved by them.</margin>
17. For if a malicious-minded witch intends to waste away the life or wealth of any miserable man or woman, she makes an image of wax. She uses the wax during an unfavorable astrological alignment <note>original: "ominous aspect"</note> that suits her design, making several magical characters upon the sides of the head. She describes the symbol of the hour or planetary time upon the breast of the image; the name of the victim on his forehead; and the intended effect to be worked upon him on his back. When they cause aches, pains, and violent pangs in the tendons <note>original: "sinews"</note> and the flesh, they stick thorns and pins in various places of the arms, breasts, and legs. When they cast them into fevers and wasting diseases <note>original: "Consumptions"</note>, they spend an hour every day warming and turning the image before a sorrowful and slow-burning fire, composed of various exotic resins <note>original: "Gums"</note>, magical ingredients of sweet odors, and strange roots of shrubs that are effective for their purpose.

<margin>Further concerning images.</margin>
18. Wonderful are the various postures and tricks which magicians play with images; I will not mention the most "perfect" and powerful parts of the practice of images and their influential operations, lest the evil-minded should work abominations with them upon the persons or possessions of their neighbors.

<margin>Of images provoking love.</margin>
19. They frame their images according to the nature of what they wish to effect. If they would use images to provoke two parties to love or be enamored with one another, they frame their images naked, with astrological observations and embraces belonging to those who are under the influence of Venus. To incite enmity, they use malignant symbols and astrological alignments, and place the images in a fighting posture.

20. If their intentions are for good, all their symbols are engraved upon the front of the body. But if they would afflict the person with a wasting disease or with death, they thrust needles through the hearts and engrave their symbols upon the buttocks or upon the shoulders, using all their conjurations in reverse and repeating every charm in the opposite way of the former.

<margin>Forms of charms in Tartary.</margin>
21. Thousands of strange and unusual charms might be described here, according to the exact form in which tradition has left them. But I have only insisted upon describing their general nature. And as the Europeans have achieved remarkable things by **images** and <term>telesms</term> <note>magical talismans or consecrated objects</note>, so the **Tartars** <note>peoples of Central Asia and North Asia</note> have wonderful ways of producing similar effects by **bottles, sheepskins, rods, basins, letters, or messages** sent to certain spirits, and many other ways unheard of in Europe.

<margin>The tying of the point.</margin>
22. As for the <term>Tying of the Point</term> <note>A charm involving tying knots in a cord or lace—the "point"—to magically prevent a man from consummating his marriage</note>, which is a strong hindrance in marital rites to restrain the secret acts between two married persons: this knot or binding has become so notorious in both practice and effect throughout France, Italy, and Spain, as well as in all the Eastern countries, that the laws of several nations have prohibited the performance of it; neither is it fit to be openly described in this place.

<margin>Charming by the sieve.</margin>
23. They have other strategies, such as **turning the sieve** with a pair of scissors <note>original: "Sizzers"; a form of divination called coscinomancy</note>, or by voices uttered out of skins (which is common among the Turks), or by letters written to certain spirits, which will have their answers returned by specific appointments.
<margin>By bottles, skins, letters, cords, lots.</margin>
They also use the **turning of the cord** with several names wrapped around it; with certain repetitions, the cord will tie itself into several strange knots which then untie themselves again. Besides these, there are many ways using **lots**, such as drawing scrolls, consulting with the **staff** <note>rhabdomancy</note> and the empty **pot**, along with others too tedious to list.

<margin>Ceremonious transplantation.</margin>
24. The art of **transplantation** is also counted among charms by the common people. And indeed one part of it—the transferring of diseases—is truly magical and much practiced among witches. For by giving certain baits to domestic beasts, they remove fevers, agues, and wasting diseases from soldiers <note>original: "Martial men"</note>, or from one person to another. By burying certain images in their neighbors' ground, they bring all evil fortune to the owner of the ground; yet

<meta>This page concludes the author's discussion on the physical instruments and materials used in magic, emphasizing their supposed "natural" basis before ending the entire discourse on spirits and charms.</meta>

...even though they include strange words and conjurations in the practice, the effects are derived more from nature than from conjuration.

<margin>And merely natural.</margin>
25. For this same reason, those who are deeply skilled can destroy diseases, remove warts and other growths <note>original: "Excrescences"</note>, and even kill, cure, purge, or poison a person from a distance. They do this using the person's hair, fat, blood, nails, or excrement, etc., or by rubbing a root or fleshy <note>original: "carnuous"</note> substance on their hands, breasts, or legs. By burying these items, they free the person from diseases; these experiments take effect based on the materials used <note>original: "Mediums"</note> and how they decay <note>original: "their Consumption"</note> underground.

<margin>Magical Instruments:</margin>
26. Just as every magical charm or recipe <note>original: "Receipt"</note> was first established through natural reasoning, magicians have also arranged the materials and methods of their tools and instruments according to the principles of nature. For example, the hour in which they make their garments must be either the hour of the Moon <note>original: "Luna"</note> or Saturn, during the Moon's increase.

<margin>Their matter,</margin>
27. They make their *garments* of white linen, black cloth, or the skins of black cats, wolves, bears, or pigs. Linen is used because of its pure <note>original: "abstracted"</note> quality, for magic does not favor tools used for common purposes. The skins of the mentioned animals are used because of the *Saturnine* <note>astrological influences associated with the planet Saturn, often linked to limitation, darkness, or death</note> and *magical qualities* found in those creatures. Their sewing thread is made of silk, catgut, human nerves, donkey hair, or leather straps made from the skins of men, cats, bats, owls, or moles—all of which are required for similar magical reasons.

<margin>Substance,</margin>
28. Their *needles* are made of hedgehog quills or the bones of the animals mentioned above. Their *writing pens* are made from owls or ravens, and their *ink* is made of human blood. Their *ointments* consist of human fat, blood, *moss from a skull* <note>original: "Usnea," a type of lichen or moss that grows on the skulls of the dead</note>, hog's grease, and whale oil. Their *characters* <note>symbolic letters or sigils</note> are ancient *Hebrew* or *Samaritan*. Their *speech* is *Hebrew* or *Latin*. Their *paper* must be made from the membranes of infants, which they call *virgin parchment*, or from the skins of cats or kids <note>young goats</note>. Furthermore, they build their *fires* using sweet wood, oil, or resin, and their *candles* are made from the fat or marrow of men or children. Their *vessels* are made of clay, and their *candlesticks* have three feet and are made from the bones of dead men. Their *swords* are steel, without handguards, and with the points reversed. These are their materials, which they choose specifically for the magical qualities of which they are composed.

<margin>And Form.</margin>
29. The specific shapes of these items also have a natural cause. Their *caps* are oval or shaped like pyramids with flaps <note>original: "Lappets"</note> on each side and fur on the inside. Their *gowns* reach the ground and are lined with white fox skins, under which they wear a linen garment reaching to the knee. Their *belts* <note>original: "Girdles"</note> are three inches wide and are inscribed with many mystical <note>original: "Caballistical"</note> names, crosses, triangles <note>original: "Trines"</note>, and circles. Their *knives* are shaped like daggers, and the *circles* they use to defend themselves are typically nine feet wide, though *Eastern magicians* use only seven feet. These are the materials and methods of their preparations, which I thought necessary to emphasize here because of their connection to the *instruments of charms*; for both, a natural cause is constantly claimed.

<margin>The Conclusion.</margin>
30. Thus, I have briefly discussed the nature of every spirit, whether *good* or *evil*, as far as safety or propriety would allow. I have also added this final discourse on *charms* and conjurations in their *theoretical* <note>original: "speculative"</note> aspect, refraining from describing the *rituals themselves*. This is because many of them are not only easy to perform but also possess great power when applied at the right time. To describe specifically how magicians kill, cure, or conquer would only empower the envious to harm the lives and fortunes of their neighbors. Therefore, readers must be satisfied with what has been shared here regarding the *nature of astral or infernal spirits*.
